title: Shivraj-Yogi High-Level Meeting: MSP Relief, 6.18 Lakh Rural Houses Approved for Uttar Pradesh
content:
Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare

Shivraj-Yogi High-Level Meeting: MSP Relief, 6.18 Lakh Rural Houses Approved for Uttar Pradesh

Major Boost for UP Farmers and Villages: Shivraj Hands Over Key Approvals to CM Yogi

MSP Procurement Extended Till July 8; 6.18 Lakh PMAY-G Houses Cleared for UP

UP Gets MSP Relief and Massive Rural Housing Push in Shivraj-Yogi Review Meeting

From Farm Security to Rural Housing: Big Decisions for Uttar Pradesh at Lucknow Meeting

Shivraj Unveils Scientific Agriculture Roadmap for UP Amid El Niño Concerns

No Field Left Fallow: Centre, UP Draw Climate-Resilient Agriculture Strategy

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUN 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Thursday held a high-level review meeting with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at Yojana Bhavan, Lucknow, to discuss the state’s agriculture and rural development scenario in detail. During the meeting, Shri Chouhan handed over two key approval letters to the Chief Minister -one extending Minimum Support Price procurement period for wheat, gram and masoor under the Rabi Marketing Season 2026–27 from June 24 to July 8, 2026, and another approving 6,18,482 pucca houses for Uttar Pradesh under the new phase of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin.

UP India’s Agricultural Flagship State, Scientific Roadmap Needed

Addressing the meeting, Shri Chouhan described Uttar Pradesh as India’s leading agricultural state, noting that the state alone contributes around 38 per cent of the country’s wheat production. “Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh has the most crucial role in ensuring India’s food security and increasing farmers’ income. Therefore, a scientific and long-term roadmap for agriculture in the state has become the need of the hour,” Chouhan said. He said climate change, rising temperatures and declining groundwater levels have emerged as serious challenges for farming. The proposed scientific roadmap for Uttar Pradesh will integrate crop patterns, irrigation, water conservation, seeds, technology and marketing strategies. A draft framework was discussed in detail with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi and their team, and will be finalized jointly by the Centre and the state government.

MSP Procurement Period Extended for Rabi 2026–27

In a major relief for farmers, the Union Agriculture Minister formally handed over the approval letter extending the MSP procurement period for key Rabi crops. The approval, granted in response to the Uttar Pradesh government’s request and keeping farmers’ interests in mind, allows procurement of wheat, gram and masoor at MSP till July 8, 2026. The extension aims to ensure that no farmer is deprived of selling produce at MSP due to practical difficulties such as weather conditions, delayed arrivals, weighing issues or congestion in mandis. The decision is expected to benefit lakhs of wheat, gram and masoor growers in Uttar Pradesh and help prevent distress sales at below-MSP prices.

El Niño Concerns: Contingency Plan for Low Rainfall

Shri Chouhan said signs of El Niño are visible this year and rainfall has so far remained below normal, with further shortfall likely. “The government’s priority is that fields should not remain vacant, farmers’ income should be protected, and the country’s food security should not be affected,” he said. Accordingly, the meeting decided to prepare district-wise contingency plans promoting short-duration and low-water-requirement crops. Alternative crop lists will be prepared based on local water availability, soil conditions and existing cropping patterns. A roadmap is also being prepared to ensure timely advisory services, seeds and technical guidance through Krishi Vigyan Kendra, the state agriculture department and local administration.

6,18,482 Rural Houses Approved Under PMAY-G

In a major push to rural housing, Shri Chouhan also handed over the approval letter sanctioning 6,18,482 pucca houses for Uttar Pradesh under the new phase of PMAY-G. He said the approval is part of the new PMAY-G phase for 2024–25 to 2028–29, under which the Centre aims to construct an additional two crore pucca houses across the country. Out of these, 6,18,482 houses have been allocated to Uttar Pradesh, opening the way for providing permanent housing to lakhs of poor rural families in a phased manner.

‘Housing for All’: Survey Completed, Focus Shifts to Delivery

Chouhan said the survey of rural households in Uttar Pradesh has been completed and eligible poor families living in kutcha houses have been identified. “The next phase is to provide priority housing to these eligible families under PMAY-G and accelerate Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Housing for All’ mission on the ground,” he said. He assured full financial and technical support from the Centre and emphasized timely construction, quality control and inclusion of every eligible beneficiary. Transparency and technology-based monitoring will be key features of implementation, he added.

Strong Team, Shared Vision

The review meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Minister and Rural Development Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi, Minister of State for Agriculture Baldev Singh Aulakh and Minister of State for Revenue Surendra Diler. Senior officials from the Union and Uttar Pradesh departments of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development also participated and gave presentations on the progress of various schemes and the ground situation. The meeting underscored that agriculture and rural development are being viewed not as isolated schemes but as a unified development vision, with emphasis on coordination and teamwork between the Centre and the Uttar Pradesh government so that policy decisions directly benefit farmers, agricultural labourers and rural poor families.

‘Farmer Strong, Villages Prosperous’: Shri Chouhan

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s clear vision is that farmers should prosper in every way and no poor family should remain without a pucca house. Both decisions, the extension of MSP procurement for Rabi 2026–27 and the approval of 6,18,482 houses under the new PMAY-G phase are linked to that vision,” Chouhan said. He said the Centre and the Uttar Pradesh government are working with a common goal: strong farmers, prosperous villages, and making Uttar Pradesh a national model for agriculture and rural development. Expressing confidence in Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and his team, Shri Chouhan said the scientific agricultural roadmap and housing programme being jointly implemented would bring major and lasting transformation to Uttar Pradesh’s farms, villages and poor families in the coming years.

# Strategic Review of Agriculture and Rural Development: Union-State Initiatives for Uttar Pradesh

## Executive Summary

On June 25, 2026, a high-level review meeting was convened at Yojana Bhavan, Lucknow, between Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The meeting focused on reinforcing Uttar Pradesh’s status as India’s agricultural flagship and accelerating rural infrastructure development.

Two landmark approvals were formalized during the session:
1.  **MSP Procurement Extension:** The deadline for Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement for Rabi crops (wheat, gram, and masoor) was extended to July 8, 2026.
2.  **PMAY-G Housing Sanction:** Approval was granted for 6,18,482 new pucca houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G).

The proceedings underscored a shift toward a scientific, climate-resilient agricultural roadmap designed to safeguard food security against El Niño-related risks and declining groundwater levels.

---

## Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. Strengthening Agricultural Resilience and Food Security
Uttar Pradesh is recognized as the central pillar of India’s food security, contributing approximately 38% of the nation's total wheat production. Given this significance, the meeting emphasized the transition from traditional practices to a "scientific and long-term roadmap."

*   **Integrated Strategy:** The proposed roadmap integrates crop patterns, irrigation, water conservation, seed technology, and marketing strategies.
*   **Climate Adaptation:** To counter rising temperatures and groundwater depletion, the Centre and State are finalizing a joint framework to ensure sustainable productivity.

### 2. Market Intervention and Financial Protection
The extension of the MSP procurement period is a strategic intervention to prevent distress sales. By moving the deadline from June 24 to July 8, 2026, the government aims to accommodate logistical challenges and ensure equitable market access for all farmers.

| Crop Category | Specific Crops Covered | New Deadline |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Rabi Marketing Season 2026–27** | Wheat, Gram, Masoor | July 8, 2026 |

**Objectives of the Extension:**
*   Mitigate delays caused by weather conditions.
*   Alleviate congestion at mandis (markets) and weighing centers.
*   Ensure no farmer is forced to sell below MSP due to practical difficulties.

### 3. Climate Contingency and El Niño Preparedness
The meeting addressed emerging concerns regarding El Niño and below-normal rainfall. To prevent fields from remaining fallow, the government is implementing a district-wise contingency plan.

*   **Alternative Cropping:** Identification of short-duration and low-water-requirement crops.
*   **Localized Advisory:** Deployment of Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and the state agriculture department to provide technical guidance and seeds based on local soil and water conditions.

### 4. Rural Infrastructure: "Housing for All"
The sanctioning of 6,18,482 pucca houses marks a major phase in the PMAY-G mission (2024–25 to 2028–29). This initiative is part of a broader national goal to construct two crore additional rural houses.

*   **Implementation Status:** Surveys of rural households in Uttar Pradesh are complete, and eligible families in kutcha houses have been identified.
*   **Delivery Standards:** The focus has shifted to transparency, quality control, and technology-based monitoring to ensure timely delivery to the most vulnerable populations.

---

## Important Quotes and Context

> **"Uttar Pradesh has the most crucial role in ensuring India’s food security and increasing farmers’ income. Therefore, a scientific and long-term roadmap for agriculture in the state has become the need of the hour."**
— *Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan regarding UP's 38% contribution to national wheat production.*

> **"The government’s priority is that fields should not remain vacant, farmers’ income should be protected, and the country’s food security should not be affected."**
— *Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on the necessity of the El Niño contingency plan.*

> **"The next phase is to provide priority housing to these eligible families under PMAY-G and accelerate Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Housing for All’ mission on the ground."**
— *Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on the transition from beneficiary identification to physical delivery of 6.18 lakh houses.*

---

## Actionable Insights and Strategic Pillars

The meeting established several critical action points for the upcoming agricultural and development cycle:

*   **District-Specific Crop Planning:** Authorities must finalize lists of alternative crops for districts facing water scarcity, prioritizing seeds that require less irrigation.
*   **Infrastructure Quality Assurance:** Implementation of PMAY-G must utilize technology-based monitoring to maintain transparency and ensure that every eligible household receives a high-quality pucca structure.
*   **Unified Development Vision:** The Centre and State have committed to viewing agriculture and rural development as a single, integrated vision rather than isolated schemes. This requires high levels of coordination between the Union and State departments.
*   **Advisory Acceleration:** Strengthening the link between Krishi Vigyan Kendras and local administration is essential for the timely delivery of technical guidance to farmers during the unpredictable 2026 monsoon season.

title: ICAR and APEDA Sea Protocol Cuts Mango Export Cost
content:
Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare

ICAR and APEDA Sea Protocol Cuts Mango Export Cost

4.3 Tonnes of Banganappalli Mangoes Shipped to Singapore by Sea with Excellent Quality Retention

ICAR-CISH Sea Shipment Technology Enhances Shelf Life of Mangoes up to 30 Days, Opening New Global Export Opportunities

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUN 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

In a major breakthrough for India’s fresh fruit export sector, Indian mangoes have successfully reached Singapore through sea shipment, marking a significant milestone in expanding affordable and large-scale mango exports to international markets.

Indian mangoes are highly valued in Singapore for their superior taste, flavour, and quality, with varieties such as Banganappalli and Kesar enjoying strong consumer demand. To make exports more economical and competitive, the ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (ICAR-CISH), Lucknow, in collaboration with APEDA, developed a scientific sea shipment protocol for mango export.

Under this initiative, a consignment of

4.3 tonnes of Banganappalli mangoes

from Andhra Pradesh was exported to Singapore through a reefer container. The sea route offers a substantial reduction in logistics costs, estimated at

₹13–20 per kg

, compared to

₹150–250 per kg

through air shipment, making exports more viable for producers and exporters while ensuring affordable prices for overseas consumers.

The protocol developed by ICAR-CISH integrates an end-to-end quality assurance system covering residue-free production, Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), scientific harvesting, grading, packing, and post-harvest management. The exported fruits underwent

Hot Water Treatment (HWT)

and

CISH-Met Wash

, an ICAR-CISH-developed technology that enhances shelf life, minimizes disease incidence, and maintains fruit quality during long-distance transportation.

The orchards were scientifically monitored by ICAR-CISH experts from fruit set to harvest using residue-safe production practices and ICAR-CISH-developed biocontrol technology

FUSICONT

. Fruits were tested for quality and Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) before processing at an APEDA-approved packhouse.

ICAR-CISH has successfully extended mango shelf life to

up to 30 days

under sea shipment conditions. The Singapore consignment completed its journey in

16 days

, and the fruits arrived in excellent condition with

20.1°Brix TSS

, nil disease incidence, and quality comparable to air-shipped mangoes.

The success of this shipment is expected to facilitate expansion of Indian mango exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and other markets, where current imports are estimated at

US$ 4–5 million

, while also creating opportunities in larger markets such as the UAE, valued at

US$ 20–25 million

.

The development of cost-effective sea shipment protocols is expected to strengthen India’s mango export ecosystem, enhance farmers’ incomes, improve export competitiveness, and promote sustainable growth of the horticulture sector.

This successful consignment marks an important step towards expanding India’s fresh mango exports through affordable and sustainable logistics solutions, benefiting farmers, exporters, and consumers worldwide.

ai_content.summary:
# Strategic Advancement in Mango Export: Implementation of ICAR-CISH Sea Shipment Protocol

## Executive Summary

The Indian mango export sector has achieved a significant milestone with the successful sea shipment of 4.3 tonnes of Banganappalli mangoes to Singapore. This achievement is the result of a collaborative effort between the ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (ICAR-CISH), Lucknow, and the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). By utilizing a newly developed scientific sea shipment protocol, the initiative has successfully extended the shelf life of mangoes to 30 days, drastically reducing logistics costs and opening new avenues for large-scale international trade. The shipment arrived in excellent condition, matching the quality of traditional air-shipped fruit while offering a more sustainable and economically viable export model.

---

## Detailed Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. Economic Transformation of Logistics
The transition from air to sea freight represents a fundamental shift in the economics of mango exports. The cost disparity between the two methods is substantial, allowing Indian mangoes to become more competitive in international markets.

| Shipping Method | Estimated Logistics Cost (per kg) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Air Shipment** | ₹150 – 250 |
| **Sea Shipment** | ₹13 – 20 |

This reduction in overhead costs benefits the entire value chain, from increasing producer and exporter margins to ensuring more affordable prices for overseas consumers.

### 2. Technological Innovation in Post-Harvest Management
The success of the 16-day journey to Singapore was predicated on advanced post-harvest technologies developed by ICAR-CISH. These interventions ensure that the fruit retains quality over long distances:
*   **Shelf Life Extension:** The protocol extends mango shelf life up to 30 days.
*   **CISH-Met Wash:** A proprietary technology used to minimize disease incidence and maintain quality during transit.
*   **Hot Water Treatment (HWT):** A standard procedure integrated into the protocol to ensure phytosanitary safety.
*   **FUSICONT:** A biocontrol technology applied during the production phase to ensure residue-safe fruit.

### 3. Comprehensive Quality Assurance Framework
The protocol is not merely a shipping method but an end-to-end quality assurance system. It begins at the orchard level and continues through to the final delivery.
*   **Production Standards:** Emphasis on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) and residue-free production.
*   **Scientific Monitoring:** Experts monitor orchards from fruit set to harvest.
*   **Testing and Certification:** Fruits undergo rigorous testing for quality and Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) at APEDA-approved packhouses before export.
*   **Quality Metrics:** The Singapore consignment recorded a Total Soluble Solids (TSS) level of 20.1°Brix and zero disease incidence upon arrival.

### 4. Market Expansion and Global Competitiveness
The successful delivery to Singapore serves as a proof-of-concept for broader market penetration. Currently, mango imports in regions like Singapore, Malaysia, and Hong Kong are estimated at US$ 4–5 million. However, the protocol opens doors to much larger markets, specifically the UAE, which is valued at US$ 20–25 million. This technological breakthrough positions India to capture a larger share of these high-value markets by offering premium varieties like Banganappalli and Kesar at sea-freight prices.

---

## Important Quotes with Context

> **"In a major breakthrough for India’s fresh fruit export sector, Indian mangoes have successfully reached Singapore through sea shipment, marking a significant milestone in expanding affordable and large-scale mango exports to international markets."**

*Context: This statement establishes the strategic importance of the shipment, framing it not just as a single delivery but as a shift toward a more scalable export model.*

> **"The sea route offers a substantial reduction in logistics costs, estimated at ₹13–20 per kg, compared to ₹150–250 per kg through air shipment, making exports more viable for producers and exporters."**

*Context: This highlights the primary economic driver behind the new protocol, emphasizing the nearly ten-fold reduction in transportation expenses.*

> **"ICAR-CISH has successfully extended mango shelf life to up to 30 days under sea shipment conditions."**

*Context: This quote identifies the specific technical achievement that enables sea transport, as traditional mango varieties often spoil before reaching distant ports via slower sea routes.*

---

## Actionable Insights

### Scale-up and Diversification
The success with Banganappalli mangoes provides a template for other varieties. Expanding the protocol to include varieties like Kesar, which also enjoys high demand, could further diversify India's export portfolio.

### Infrastructure Optimization
To replicate this success, there is a clear need to utilize APEDA-approved packhouses and ensure the availability of reefer containers. Stakeholders should focus on integrating CISH-Met Wash and HWT facilities into standard export hubs.

### Targeted Market Entry
Exporters should prioritize markets in Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Hong Kong) and the Middle East (UAE). Given the US$ 20–25 million value of the UAE market, focusing on sea-shipment logistics to this region could yield the highest return on investment.

### Farmer Training and Adoption
To meet the rigorous standards required for sea shipment, local farmers must be trained in Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) and the use of biocontrol technologies like FUSICONT. Ensuring "residue-free" production is critical for passing MRL tests required for international trade.

# Briefing Document: Official Visit of Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan to Karnataka

## Executive Summary

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, is scheduled to undertake a two-day official visit to Karnataka on June 27 and June 28, 2026. Centered in Bengaluru, the visit focuses on two distinct thematic pillars: the celebration of regional historical heritage and the promotion of public health through national social welfare initiatives. The itinerary includes the commemoration of the 517th birth anniversary of Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda and participation in a high-level conclave dedicated to the "Nasha Mukt Bharat" (Drug-Free India) campaign.

## Detailed Itinerary and Analysis of Key Themes

The Vice-President’s visit is structured around two major events that highlight the intersection of cultural legacy and contemporary social challenges.

### 1. Commemoration of Regional Heritage (June 27, 2026)
The first day of the visit is dedicated to the **517th Birth Anniversary Celebrations of Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda**. 

*   **Significance:** Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda is traditionally recognized as the founder of Bengaluru. The Vice-President's attendance at this celebration underscores the importance of honoring historical figures who shaped the urban and cultural landscape of the region.
*   **Location:** Bengaluru, Karnataka.

### 2. Public Health and Social Advocacy (June 28, 2026)
On the second day, the Vice-President will engage with academic and social welfare institutions during the **Nasha Mukt Bharat Conclave**.

*   **Institutional Context:** The conclave is organized as a dual-purpose event:
    *   Commemoration of the **Foundation Day of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS)**.
    *   Observation of the **International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking**.
*   **Thematic Focus:** The "Nasha Mukt Bharat" initiative is a national campaign aimed at eradicating drug abuse. By participating in this program at a health-focused university (RGUHS), the Vice-President’s visit emphasizes the role of educational and medical institutions in addressing substance abuse and illicit trafficking.

---

---

## Important Quotes and Contextual Significance

The following details from the official release provide context for the Vice-Presidential engagement:

*   **Context of the Visit:** *"The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will be on a two-day visit to Karnataka from June 27 to 28, 2026."*

    *   *Significance:* This aligns the Vice-Presidential visit with global efforts to combat drug abuse, framing the local event within a broader international and national policy context.

---

## Actionable Insights

Based on the planned itinerary, the following insights are relevant for stakeholders involved in the visit:

*   **Promotion of Regional Identity:** The Vice-President’s participation in the Kempegowda celebrations serves as a significant gesture of recognition for Karnataka’s local history, providing an opportunity for the administration to strengthen ties with regional cultural organizations.

This suggests that public health and the fight against drug abuse remain top-tier priorities for the executive branch.
*   **Strategic Communication:** The visit utilizes a major historical anniversary and an international awareness day to maximize public outreach and reinforce the government's stance on both cultural preservation and social reform.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the contributions of Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda to urban planning and administration, particularly in the context of Bengaluru. How relevant are his principles in contemporary urban development?
mains_questions.answer:
Introduction:
Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda I, a chieftain under the Vijayanagara Empire, is credited with founding the city of Bengaluru in the 16th century. His vision laid the groundwork for a well-planned and prosperous urban center.

Contributions to Urban Planning and Administration:
1.  **Strategic Location and Layout:** He chose a strategic elevated plateau for Bengaluru and marked its boundaries with four watchtowers, envisioning a defensible and expandable city.
2.  **Planned Settlements (Petes):** He established various 'petes' (localities) dedicated to specific trades and communities, such as Doddapete (main market), Chikpete (small market), and other specialized areas, fostering economic activity and organized living.
3.  **Water Management:** Kempegowda was instrumental in constructing numerous tanks (lakes) like Dharmambudhi, Kempambudhi, and Siddikatte, crucial for meeting the city's water needs and supporting agriculture.
4.  **Fortification and Infrastructure:** He built a mud fort and laid out roads, temples, and public spaces, providing essential infrastructure for the nascent city.
5.  **Administrative Foresight:** His administration encouraged trade, ensured law and order, and promoted a vibrant cultural environment, attracting people and fostering growth.

Relevance in Contemporary Urban Development:
1.  **Integrated Planning:** Kempegowda's holistic approach to urban development, integrating residential, commercial, and water resources, offers lessons for modern master planning to avoid haphazard growth.
2.  **Sustainable Water Management:** The emphasis on creating and maintaining water bodies is highly relevant today amidst urban water crises. Revival and protection of lakes are critical for urban sustainability.
3.  **Decentralized Economic Hubs:** The 'pete' system, with its specialized markets, can be seen as an early form of decentralized economic zones, reducing congestion in a single central business district.
4.  **Green Spaces and Heritage Preservation:** His vision included open spaces and cultural sites. Contemporary urban planning must prioritize green infrastructure and the preservation of historical and cultural heritage.
5.  **Community-Centric Development:** The organic growth around specific trades fostered a sense of community, a principle that can be applied to create livable and inclusive neighborhoods today.

Conclusion:
Nadaprabhu Sri Kempegowda's legacy extends beyond the founding of Bengaluru; his principles of planned development, sustainable resource management, and community-centric growth remain remarkably relevant. Understanding and adapting these historical insights can guide contemporary urban planners in building resilient, equitable, and sustainable cities for the future.

mains_questions.question: Critically evaluate the objectives and implementation of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) in addressing the challenge of drug abuse in India. What further measures are needed to achieve a drug-free society?
mains_questions.answer:
Introduction:
Drug abuse poses a significant public health and social challenge in India, impacting individuals, families, and society at large. The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched in 2020, is a flagship initiative by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to tackle this growing menace.

Objectives of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan:
1.  **Awareness Generation:** To increase public awareness about the ill effects of substance abuse, particularly among youth and vulnerable populations.
2.  **Focus on Vulnerable Districts:** To concentrate efforts in 272 identified districts most affected by substance abuse.
3.  **Treatment and Rehabilitation:** To strengthen the existing treatment and rehabilitation infrastructure and facilitate access to services.
4.  **Community Participation:** To mobilize community support and encourage participation from various stakeholders, including educational institutions, NGOs, and local bodies.
5.  **Capacity Building:** To train frontline workers and service providers to effectively address substance abuse issues.

Critical Evaluation of Implementation:
Strengths:
*   **Wide Outreach:** The Abhiyaan has successfully engaged a large number of volunteers and institutions, conducting extensive awareness campaigns.
*   **Data-Driven Approach:** The focus on identified vulnerable districts allows for targeted interventions based on prevalence data.
*   **Youth Engagement:** Significant efforts have been made to involve youth and educational institutions, crucial for prevention.
*   **Digital Integration:** Use of digital platforms and apps for awareness and monitoring has enhanced reach.

Weaknesses/Challenges:
*   **Stigma and Discrimination:** Despite awareness, the social stigma associated with drug abuse often deters individuals from seeking help.
*   **Limited Rehabilitation Infrastructure:** The availability and accessibility of quality de-addiction and rehabilitation centers, especially in rural areas, remain inadequate.
*   **Cross-Border Trafficking:** India's geographical location makes it vulnerable to illicit drug trafficking, which undermines domestic efforts.
*   **Lack of Sustained Follow-up:** Long-term follow-up and aftercare services are often insufficient, leading to high relapse rates.
*   **Integration with Mental Health:** The strong link between substance abuse and mental health issues is not always adequately addressed in integrated treatment plans.
*   **Enforcement Gaps:** While awareness is crucial, effective law enforcement against drug peddlers and suppliers is equally vital.

Further Measures Needed to Achieve a Drug-Free Society:
1.  **Strengthening Law Enforcement:** Enhance intelligence gathering, border surveillance, and inter-agency coordination to curb drug supply.
2.  **Comprehensive Mental Health Integration:** Develop integrated treatment models that address co-occurring mental health disorders alongside substance abuse.
3.  **Expand and Improve Rehabilitation:** Increase the number of quality de-addiction and rehabilitation centers, ensuring accessibility, affordability, and evidence-based practices.
4.  **Targeted Prevention Programs:** Develop age-appropriate and culturally sensitive prevention programs for specific vulnerable groups, including children and adolescents.
5.  **Addressing Root Causes:** Tackle socio-economic factors like unemployment, poverty, and lack of opportunities that contribute to substance abuse.
6.  **International Cooperation:** Strengthen collaboration with neighboring countries and international agencies to combat cross-border drug trafficking.
7.  **Research and Data:** Invest in research to understand evolving drug abuse patterns and develop effective intervention strategies.
8.  **Public-Private Partnerships:** Encourage greater involvement of the private sector and NGOs in prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts.

Conclusion:
The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is a commendable step towards addressing drug abuse. However, achieving a truly drug-free society requires a multi-pronged, sustained, and integrated approach that combines robust law enforcement, accessible healthcare, comprehensive rehabilitation, and proactive community engagement, while also addressing the underlying socio-economic determinants.

title: Prime Minister congratulates Abelardo de la Espriella on his victory in the Colombian presidential elections

Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister congratulates Abelardo de la Espriella on his victory in the Colombian presidential elections

Posted On:
                26 JUN 2026 10:47PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi congratulated Abelardo de la Espriella on his victory in the Colombian presidential elections.

The Prime Minister noted that India deeply  values its close friendship with Colombia which continues to grow in all areas. “I convey my best wishes for a successful tenure and look forward to working together to further deepen our bilateral relations in the years ahead”, Shri Modi added.

Shri Modi posted on X;

Heartiest congratulations, Abelardo de la Espriella, on your victory in the Colombian presidential elections.

India values its close friendship with Colombia which continues to grow in all areas. I convey my best wishes for a successful tenure and look forward to working together to further deepen our bilateral relations in the years ahead.

@ABDELAESPRIELLA

Heartiest congratulations, Abelardo de la Espriella, on your victory in the Colombian presidential elections.

India values its close friendship with Colombia which continues to grow in all areas. I convey my best wishes for a successful tenure and look forward to working…

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi)

June 26, 2026

***

MJPS/SS/VJ

(Release ID: 2278332)

Introduction: Briefly set the context of India's evolving foreign policy, which seeks to expand its global footprint beyond traditional partners, with a growing focus on regions like Latin America, exemplified by the recent outreach to Colombia.

Opportunities in Deepening Relations:
*   **Economic Complementarity:** Latin America offers resources (oil, minerals, agricultural products) and markets, while India provides IT services, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing expertise.
*   **Diversification of Partnerships:** Reduces over-reliance on traditional partners, enhances India's strategic autonomy.
*   **South-South Cooperation:** Strengthens solidarity among developing nations on global platforms.
*   **Geopolitical Influence:** Enhances India's standing as a global player by expanding its diplomatic reach.
*   **Technological Collaboration:** Potential for joint ventures in space, renewable energy, and digital technologies.

Challenges in Deepening Relations:
*   **Geographical Distance and Connectivity:** Long shipping routes, limited direct air connectivity, increasing logistics costs.
*   **Language and Cultural Barriers:** Spanish and Portuguese are dominant, requiring dedicated efforts for communication and understanding.
*   **Lack of Awareness:** Limited understanding of each other's markets, cultures, and political systems.
*   **Competition from Other Powers:** Strong presence of China, USA, and European powers in the region.
*   **Political and Economic Instability:** Some countries in the region face internal political challenges or economic volatility, posing risks for investment.
*   **Infrastructure Deficiencies:** Inadequate port infrastructure and internal transport networks in some Latin American countries.

Examples:
*   **Opportunities:** India's oil imports from Venezuela, agricultural trade with Brazil and Argentina, IT services to Mexico, pharmaceutical exports to various countries, recent engagement with Colombia.
*   **Challenges:** Limited direct flights, language barriers in business negotiations, competition from Chinese investments in infrastructure.

Conclusion: Conclude by emphasizing that despite the challenges, the strategic and economic imperatives for India to deepen ties with Latin America are significant. Suggest proactive measures like enhanced diplomatic outreach, targeted trade missions, improved connectivity, and cultural exchange programs to overcome hurdles and unlock the full potential of these partnerships.

title: Prime Minister pays homage to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on his jayanti
content:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister pays homage to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on his jayanti

Posted On:
                26 JUN 2026 12:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, today, paid tributes to the great Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on his Jayanti, remembering him as a towering literary luminary whose writings ignited the spirit of patriotism and cultural pride among generations of Indians.

Highlighting the significance of the year, Shri Modi noted that India is commemorating the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram. He remarked that through Vande Mataram, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay gifted the Indian freedom movement and the nation one of its most enduring sources of inspiration.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

Tributes to the great Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on his Jayanti.

A towering literary luminary, his writings awakened a spirit of patriotism and cultural pride among generations of Indians. His rich literary work continues to illuminate minds and strengthen our collective resolve towards nation-building.

This is a time when we are marking the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram. Through Vande Mataram, he gifted the freedom movement and our nation one of its most enduring inspirations.

ai_content.summary:
# The Legacy of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay: Commemorating 150 Years of Vande Mataram

## Executive Summary

On June 26, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on the occasion of his Jayanti (birth anniversary). The Prime Minister characterized Chattopadhyay as a "towering literary luminary" whose work has been fundamental in shaping India's national identity. A central focus of this year's tribute is the 150th anniversary of *Vande Mataram*, a composition identified as one of the most enduring sources of inspiration for the Indian freedom movement. The Prime Minister’s message emphasizes that Chattopadhyay’s literary contributions continue to illuminate the national consciousness and strengthen the collective resolve toward contemporary nation-building.

## Analysis of Key Themes

The official communication highlights several core themes regarding the influence and legacy of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

### 1. Literary Influence and Cultural Pride
The Prime Minister identifies Chattopadhyay not merely as an author but as a "literary luminary" whose writings transcended simple storytelling. His work is credited with:
*   **Awakening Patriotism:** Igniting a sense of duty and love for the country across multiple generations.
*   **Instilling Cultural Pride:** Fostering a deep-seated appreciation for Indian culture and heritage.
*   **Illuminating Minds:** Providing intellectual and emotional clarity through rich literary output.

### 2. The Significance of Vande Mataram
The year 2026 marks the 150th anniversary of *Vande Mataram*. The document positions this specific work as a pivotal gift to the nation, noting:
*   **Historical Impact:** It served as a primary catalyst and source of inspiration during the Indian freedom movement.
*   **Enduring Legacy:** It remains a foundational element of the national spirit, continuing to resonate 150 years after its inception.

### 3. Nation-Building and Collective Resolve
The tribute connects historical literary achievements to modern national objectives. The Prime Minister suggests that reflecting on Chattopadhyay’s work is essential for:
*   **Strengthening Resolve:** Enhancing the unified determination of the citizenry to contribute to the nation’s growth.
*   **Guiding Future Generations:** Ensuring that the spirit of patriotism awakened in the past continues to drive the country's progress today.

## Important Quotes and Context

The following table outlines key statements made by the Prime Minister and their significance within the context of the national tribute.

| Quote | Context/Significance |
| :--- | :--- |
| "A towering literary luminary, his writings awakened a spirit of patriotism and cultural pride among generations of Indians." | Establishes Chattopadhyay as a foundational figure in the development of Indian national identity and intellectual history. |
| "Through Vande Mataram, he gifted the freedom movement and our nation one of its most enduring inspirations." | Highlights the specific role of *Vande Mataram* as a tool for mobilization and a permanent symbol of the Indian spirit. |
| "His rich literary work continues to illuminate minds and strengthen our collective resolve towards nation-building." | Transitions the historical legacy of the author into a modern context, emphasizing its ongoing relevance to current national goals. |
| "This is a time when we are marking the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram." | Provides the specific temporal context for the 2026 Jayanti, elevating the observance to a major national milestone. |

## Actionable Insights

Based on the Prime Minister's address and the significance of the 150th anniversary of *Vande Mataram*, the following insights are derived:

*   **Commemorative Focus:** National attention is directed toward the 150th anniversary of *Vande Mataram*, suggesting a period of reflection on the song's role in the freedom struggle and its place in modern India.
*   **Educational Emphasis:** There is a clear mandate to revisit and promote the "rich literary work" of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay to ensure it continues to "illuminate minds" of younger generations.
*   **Unity through Heritage:** The use of Chattopadhyay’s legacy serves as a tool for fostering "collective resolve," suggesting that cultural and literary heritage should be leveraged to unify the nation in its current nation-building efforts.
*   **Multilingual Outreach:** The dissemination of this tribute in multiple languages (including Urdu, Marathi, Hindi, Manipuri, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam) underscores the intended pan-Indian reach of Chattopadhyay’s influence.

mains_questions.question: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's literary contributions were instrumental in awakening a spirit of patriotism and cultural pride during the Indian freedom struggle. Discuss his role, with particular reference to 'Vande Mataram'.
mains_questions.answer:
Introduction:
Briefly introduce Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay as a prominent literary figure and nationalist during the 19th century, known for his profound impact on Indian thought and the freedom movement.

Body Paragraph 1: Literary Contributions and Nationalism:
*   His novels, such as 'Anandamath', 'Durgeshnandini', and 'Kapalkundala', were not merely literary works but vehicles for nationalist ideas and social commentary.
*   He critiqued social evils, advocated for national regeneration, and highlighted the glory of India's past.
*   His writings helped in shaping modern Bengali prose and literature, influencing subsequent generations of writers and thinkers.

Body Paragraph 2: 'Vande Mataram' - A Symbol of Patriotism:
*   'Vande Mataram', originally a poem in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882), quickly transcended its literary context to become a powerful national anthem.
*   It depicted the motherland as a divine entity, inspiring deep emotional attachment and devotion among Indians.
*   Its adoption as a rallying cry during the Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908) and other phases of the freedom struggle made it an enduring symbol of resistance against British rule.
*   The song instilled a strong sense of cultural pride and a unified national identity, transcending linguistic and regional barriers.

Conclusion:
Summarize Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's enduring legacy as a literary giant and a catalyst for Indian nationalism. His works, especially 'Vande Mataram', continue to inspire patriotism and cultural pride, making him an indispensable figure in India's freedom struggle and cultural renaissance.

mains_questions.question: How did literary figures like Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay contribute to the cultural awakening and the growth of nationalism in 19th-century India? Elaborate with suitable examples.
mains_questions.answer:
Introduction:
The 19th century in India was a period of significant socio-religious reforms and the nascent stages of nationalism. Literary figures played a pivotal role in fostering a cultural awakening and shaping the nationalist discourse.

Body Paragraph 1: Role of Literature in Cultural Awakening:
*   **Revival of Indigenous Languages and Forms:** Writers promoted vernacular languages, making literature accessible to a wider audience and fostering regional identities that eventually fed into a larger national identity.
*   **Critique of Colonial Policies and Social Injustices:** Through novels, plays, and essays, authors exposed the exploitative nature of British rule and challenged prevailing social evils like caste discrimination, sati, and child marriage.
*   **Promotion of Indian History and Values:** Literary works often glorified India's ancient past, its rich cultural heritage, and traditional values, instilling a sense of pride and self-respect among the populace. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's historical novels are prime examples.

Body Paragraph 2: Literature and Growth of Nationalism:
*   **Instilling a Sense of Shared Identity:** By creating narratives that resonated with common experiences and aspirations, writers helped forge a collective consciousness and a sense of belonging to a larger Indian nation.
*   **Inspiring Resistance:** Works like Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 'Anandamath' and its iconic song 'Vande Mataram' directly inspired revolutionary activities and mass movements, providing emotional and ideological fuel for the freedom struggle.
*   **Creating a Common Platform for Discourse:** Literary journals and publications became crucial platforms for discussing political ideas, social reforms, and nationalist aspirations, uniting intellectuals and activists across regions.
*   **Examples:** Besides Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, figures like Rabindranath Tagore (later), Bharatendu Harishchandra, and Dinabandhu Mitra used their literary prowess to awaken national consciousness and advocate for social change.

Conclusion:
Conclude by emphasizing the profound and multifaceted impact of literary figures in shaping the intellectual and emotional landscape that fueled the Indian nationalist movement and cultural renaissance. Their writings served as both a mirror reflecting the societal realities and a torch guiding the path towards self-rule and national identity.

ai_content.summary:
# Tribute to Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj: Commemorative Briefing

## Executive Summary

On June 26, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid formal tribute to Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj on the occasion of his birth anniversary. The tribute, disseminated through official channels and social media, underscores Shahu Ji Maharaj's enduring legacy as a pioneer of social reform in India. The Prime Minister’s remarks centered on Maharaj’s lifelong commitment to the "upliftment of the deprived, exploited, and backward classes," positioning his ideals as a perpetual guiding force for the nation’s progress toward social justice and equality.

## Analysis of Key Themes

The official communications regarding this tribute highlight three primary themes that define the historical and contemporary relevance of Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj.

### 1. Lifelong Commitment to the Marginalized
A central tenet of the Prime Minister’s message is the absolute dedication Shahu Ji Maharaj showed toward the "deprived, exploited, and backward classes." His life’s work is characterized not as a series of isolated acts, but as a total devotion to improving the socio-economic status of those on the fringes of society.

### 2. Advocacy for Social Justice and Equality
The tribute identifies Maharaj as a "strong advocate of social justice and equality." By framing his legacy in these terms, the communication emphasizes the foundational nature of his work in building a fair society. This advocacy is presented as the cornerstone of his public life and his most significant contribution to the Indian socio-political fabric.

### 3. National Guidance and Eternal Relevance
The Prime Minister’s remarks suggest that Shahu Ji Maharaj’s influence is not confined to the past. By stating that his "great deeds and ideals will continue to guide the nation for ages to come," the tribute elevates Maharaj from a historical figure to a permanent moral and ideological compass for the country.

## Important Quotes and Context

The following quotes from Prime Minister Narendra Modi provide the primary sentiment and official stance on the legacy of Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj.

| Quote | Context |
| :--- | :--- |
| "He dedicated his life to the upliftment of the deprived, exploited, and backward classes." | Delivered as part of the official tribute to mark the birth anniversary, highlighting the target demographics of Maharaj’s reforms. |
| "His great deeds and ideals will continue to guide the nation for ages to come." | A reflection on the long-term impact of Maharaj’s work on India's national trajectory and future governance. |
| "He was a strong advocate of social justice and equality." | (Translated from Hindi/Marathi posts) Summarizing the core values that drove Maharaj's administrative and social initiatives. |

## Actionable Insights

Based on the official sentiments expressed in the tribute, several key insights regarding the national perspective on social reform can be identified:

*   **Prioritization of Social Equity:** The emphasis on the "upliftment of the deprived" suggests that the ideals of Shahu Ji Maharaj remain a benchmark for evaluating contemporary social welfare and justice programs.
*   **Ideological Continuity:** The tribute reinforces the importance of historical reformers in shaping modern national identity. Using Maharaj's "ideals" as a guide suggests a continued state commitment to the principles of equality he championed.
*   **Multilingual Outreach:** The release of this tribute in multiple languages (including Urdu, Hindi, Marathi, Manipuri, Bengali, Assamese, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam) underscores the importance of disseminating the message of social justice across diverse linguistic and regional demographics to ensure national resonance.

mains_questions.question: “Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj dedicated his life to the upliftment of the deprived, exploited, and backward classes.” Elaborate on his significant contributions as a social reformer and a proponent of equality. (150 words)
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj (1874-1922) was a visionary ruler of Kolhapur and a towering figure in India's social reform movement, renowned for his unwavering commitment to social justice and equality.

**Contributions:**
*   **Pioneer of Reservation:** In 1902, he implemented a reservation policy, reserving 50% of government jobs for backward classes, a revolutionary step for its time, aiming to ensure their representation and upliftment.
*   **Educational Empowerment:** He actively promoted education for all, especially for the marginalized. He established numerous schools for untouchables and backward classes, made primary education compulsory and free, and provided hostels and financial aid to students from deprived backgrounds.
*   **Eradication of Untouchability:** Shahu Ji Maharaj vehemently opposed untouchability. He opened public wells, temples, and schools to all castes, and appointed individuals from lower castes to significant administrative positions, challenging traditional hierarchies.
*   **Agrarian Reforms:** He introduced reforms to protect farmers and tenants from exploitation, ensuring better land rights and fairer revenue collection.
*   **Promotion of Inter-caste Marriages:** He encouraged inter-caste marriages to break down caste barriers and foster social cohesion.

**Conclusion:** Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj's radical reforms laid the groundwork for affirmative action and social justice policies in independent India. His legacy continues to inspire efforts towards creating an inclusive and equitable society.

mains_questions.question: “The ideals of Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj regarding social justice and equality continue to guide the nation for ages to come.” Discuss the contemporary relevance of his principles in addressing socio-economic disparities in India. (250 words)
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj's principles of social justice, equality, and empowerment of the marginalized remain profoundly relevant in contemporary India, a nation still grappling with socio-economic disparities.

**Contemporary Relevance:**
*   **Affirmative Action Policies:** His pioneering work in implementing reservations directly influenced the constitutional provisions for affirmative action in India. The ongoing debates and implementation of reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes reflect the continued need for such measures to ensure equitable representation and address historical injustices.
*   **Inclusive Education:** Shahu Ji Maharaj's emphasis on universal and accessible education for all, particularly the deprived, resonates with current government initiatives like the Right to Education Act and various scholarship schemes aimed at bringing marginalized sections into the educational mainstream.
*   **Combating Discrimination:** His relentless fight against untouchability and caste-based discrimination finds its modern parallel in laws like the Protection of Civil Rights Act and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, which aim to eradicate discrimination and promote social harmony.
*   **Empowerment of Vulnerable Sections:** His broader vision for the upliftment of the exploited and backward classes aligns with contemporary policies focused on inclusive growth, poverty alleviation, and targeted welfare programs for women, farmers, and other vulnerable groups.
*   **Social Cohesion:** His efforts to break down caste barriers and promote inter-caste harmony are crucial in a diverse society still facing communal and caste-based tensions, emphasizing the need for unity and mutual respect.

**Conclusion:** Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj's ideals provide a robust framework for addressing persistent socio-economic inequalities. His legacy serves as a constant reminder that true national progress hinges on ensuring justice, dignity, and equal opportunities for every citizen.

# Analysis of the Prime Minister’s Communiqué on Unity and Mutual Harmony

## Executive Summary

On June 26, 2026, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) issued a formal release regarding a message shared by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The communication centers on a "Sanskrit Subhashitam"—a traditional aphorism or verse—aimed at promoting the values of unity and mutual harmony within society. By utilizing a classical Sanskrit verse on a modern social media platform (X), the Prime Minister emphasized the necessity of collective action and synchronized thought. The message was disseminated widely through the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Delhi and made available in twelve regional languages, reflecting a strategic effort to ensure the message reached a diverse, multilingual audience.

## Detailed Analysis of Key Themes

The communication from the Prime Minister’s Office highlights several core themes related to social governance and cultural identity.

### 1. The Principle of Collective Unity (Sangaṭṭhadhvam)
The primary theme of the communiqué is the importance of "working together." The shared verse serves as a call for collective movement and action. By advocating for unity, the message suggests that social progress is rooted in the ability of individuals to align their efforts toward common goals.

### 2. Mutual Harmony and Shared Understanding (Saṃvada-dhvam)
Beyond mere physical cooperation, the message emphasizes "mutual harmony." This involves not only acting together but also speaking and thinking in unison. The analysis of the Subhashitam indicates that true harmony is achieved when "minds are in agreement," suggesting that psychological and intellectual alignment is a prerequisite for a stable and cooperative society.

### 3. Cultural Continuity and Traditional Wisdom
The use of a Sanskrit Subhashitam signifies a reliance on traditional wisdom to address contemporary social dynamics. By referencing "Sanskrit Subhashitam," the Prime Minister utilizes historical philosophical frameworks to reinforce modern values of citizenship and social cohesion. This underscores a theme of cultural continuity, where ancient verses are positioned as relevant guides for modern behavior.

### 4. Multilingual Outreach and Accessibility
A significant aspect of this communication is its broad accessibility. The release was translated into numerous languages, ensuring the message of unity was not confined to a single linguistic group.

| Language Category | Languages Included in Release |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Northern/Central** | Hindi, Urdu |
| **Western** | Marathi, Gujarati |
| **Southern** | Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada |
| **Eastern/North-Eastern** | Manipuri, Bengali, Assamese, Odia |

## Important Quotes and Context

The following Sanskrit verse serves as the centerpiece of the Prime Minister’s message, shared via the social media platform X.

> **“सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्। देवा भागं यथा पूर्वे सञ्जानाना उपासते॥”**

### Contextual Significance
*   **Sङ्गच्छध्वं (Saṃgacchadhvaṃ):** "May you move together." This provides the context for physical and social mobilization toward a shared destination or objective.
*   **संवदध्वं (Saṃvadadhvaṃ):** "May you speak together." This suggests the importance of dialogue and reaching a consensus.
*   **सं वो मनांसि जानताम् (Saṃ vo manāṃsi jānatām):** "May your minds be in agreement." This is the foundational requirement for the harmony mentioned in the PMO release.
*   **Historical Reference:** The latter half of the verse ("देवा भागं यथा पूर्वे...") refers to the manner in which the divine or ancient entities accepted their shares in unity, providing a mythological or historical precedent for the behavior being encouraged.

## Actionable Insights

Based on the documentation of the Prime Minister's message, the following insights can be derived regarding the intended impact and administrative strategy:

*   **Emphasis on Shared Purpose:** The communication indicates that the leadership views unity not just as a sentiment, but as an active requirement for progress ("one should always work together").
*   **Utilization of Digital Platforms for Cultural Diplomacy:** The use of 'X' (formerly Twitter) to share Sanskrit verses demonstrates a strategy of using modern technology to propagate traditional values, making them accessible to a digitally active populace.
*   **Standardization of Social Values:** By sharing the same verse in multiple languages, the administration seeks to create a standardized value system across diverse regions, emphasizing that the need for harmony transcends linguistic and regional boundaries.
*   **Promotion of Dialogue:** The specific inclusion of "संवदध्वं" (speaking together) suggests an emphasis on communication as a tool for resolving differences and maintaining social order.

title: DAE Inaugurates World's First Hydrogen Production Facility Based on Copper–Chlorine Thermochemical Cycle Using Nuclear Heat from Fast Breeder Test Reactor
content:
Department of Atomic Energy

DAE Inaugurates World's First Hydrogen Production Facility Based on Copper–Chlorine Thermochemical Cycle Using Nuclear Heat from Fast Breeder Test Reactor

World's first Copper–Chlorine thermochemical hydrogen production facility using nuclear heat from FBTR

Built upon the unique capabilities of FBTR, India's only operating fast reactor research facility

Demonstrates IGCAR's leadership in advanced reactor technologies and innovative non-electric applications of nuclear energy

Showcases the successful translation of BARC's indigenously developed Copper–Chlorine thermochemical hydrogen production technology

Advances India's three-stage nuclear programme by expanding the role of nuclear energy beyond electricity generation into clean hydrogen production

Posted On:
                26 JUN 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

In a landmark achievement for India's clean energy and advanced nuclear technology programme, the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) today inaugurated the world's first Hydrogen Production Facility based on the Copper–Chlorine (Cu–Cl) Thermochemical Cycle utilizing nuclear process heat generated from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), Kalpakkam. The facility was inaugurated by Dr. Ajit Kumar Mohanty, Secretary, DAE & Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission (AEC), in the presence of Shri Sreekumar G. Pillai, Director, IGCAR.

The facility has been established as a technology demonstrator to validate the production of hydrogen using nuclear energy through the Cu–Cl thermochemical process developed indigenously by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Mumbai. The successful integration of nuclear process heat with hydrogen generation marks a pioneering technological breakthrough and opens a promising pathway for large-scale, carbon-free hydrogen production using advanced nuclear reactors.

Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key energy carrier for the future and is expected to play a pivotal role in the global transition towards clean and sustainable energy systems. Among the various hydrogen production technologies under development worldwide, the Cu–Cl thermochemical cycle is considered one of the most promising due to its relatively lower operating temperatures and higher thermodynamic efficiency. By harnessing nuclear heat from fast reactors, the process significantly reduces dependence on fossil fuels and eliminates greenhouse gas emissions associated with conventional hydrogen production methods.

The commissioning of the facility represents the culmination of extensive research, process development, engineering design, equipment fabrication, installation, testing and commissioning efforts undertaken jointly by BARC and IGCAR. The plant will provide valuable operational experience, facilitate further optimization of the Cu–Cl process and support future research aimed at scaling up nuclear-assisted hydrogen production technologies for commercial deployment.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Ajit Kumar Mohanty said,

"The integration of nuclear energy with emerging clean energy technologies such as hydrogen production represents a strategic pathway towards a sustainable energy future. Nuclear power, with its unique ability to provide reliable carbon-free electricity as well as high-temperature process heat, is ideally suited to support large-scale hydrogen production while contributing to India's energy security, decarbonization goals and long-term sustainable development objectives. I congratulate the scientists, engineers and technical teams of BARC and IGCAR whose sustained dedication, innovation and technical excellence have transformed an advanced scientific concept into an operational reality. This achievement is a testament to India's growing capabilities in advanced nuclear technologies and clean energy systems."

IGCAR, one of India's premier nuclear research institutions under the Department of Atomic Energy, has been at the forefront of the country's Fast Breeder Reactor programme since its establishment in 1971. The Centre successfully designed, constructed and operated the Fast Breeder Test Reactor, which has served as an invaluable platform for the development and validation of fuels, materials and sodium technologies for more than four decades. The knowledge and expertise generated through FBTR have laid the technological foundation for India's fast reactor programme and played a pivotal role in the development of the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), the flagship of the second stage of India's three-stage nuclear power programme.

Shri Sreekumar G. Pillai, Director, IGCAR, said,

"This achievement builds upon more than four decades of operational experience and technological excellence gained through the Fast Breeder Test Reactor programme at IGCAR. The successful demonstration of hydrogen production using nuclear process heat showcases the versatility of advanced nuclear systems and underscores IGCAR's commitment to developing innovative technologies that contribute to India's clean energy transition and long-term energy security."

Over the years, IGCAR has established internationally recognised capabilities in reactor physics, thermal hydraulics, advanced materials, sodium technology, fuel cycle research, instrumentation and control systems, remote handling, non-destructive evaluation and high-temperature engineering. Its contributions continue to strengthen India's technological self-reliance and reinforce the nation's position among the global leaders in advanced nuclear technologies.

The inauguration of the facility marks a major step towards realizing the vision of AtmaNirbhar Bharat through the convergence of nuclear energy and clean hydrogen technologies. It demonstrates DAE's continued commitment to indigenous innovation and reinforces India's resolve to build a sustainable, secure and low-carbon energy future for Viksit Bharat.

# Inauguration of the World’s First Nuclear-Assisted Copper–Chlorine Thermochemical Hydrogen Production Facility

## Executive Summary

On June 26, 2026, the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) inaugurated a landmark facility at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in Kalpakkam, marking the world’s first successful integration of a Copper–Chlorine (Cu–Cl) thermochemical cycle with nuclear process heat from a Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR). This facility serves as a technological demonstrator, validating an indigenously developed process by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) for carbon-free hydrogen production. 

The project represents a significant shift in the application of nuclear energy, moving beyond traditional electricity generation to address the global demand for clean energy carriers. By utilizing the high-temperature process heat generated by the FBTR, the facility achieves high thermodynamic efficiency and reduces reliance on fossil fuels. This achievement reinforces India’s leadership in advanced reactor technologies and supports the nation’s strategic goals for energy security, decarbonization, and the realization of a "Viksit Bharat" (Developed India).

---

## Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. Technological Innovation and Indigenous Development
The facility is the result of a collaborative effort between two of India’s premier nuclear institutions:
*   **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC):** Responsible for the indigenous development of the Copper–Chlorine (Cu–Cl) thermochemical hydrogen production technology.
*   **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR):** Provided the operational platform via the Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) and managed the engineering design, installation, and commissioning.

This synergy demonstrates a successful transition from an advanced scientific concept to an operational reality, showcasing India’s ability to design, fabricate, and test complex nuclear-integrated systems.

### 2. Diversification of Nuclear Energy Applications
Traditionally, nuclear energy in India has been synonymous with electricity generation. This facility expands the role of the country’s three-stage nuclear programme by demonstrating "non-electric" applications. By harnessing nuclear heat for chemical processes, the DAE is positioning nuclear power as a versatile tool for industrial decarbonization.

### 3. Advantages of the Cu–Cl Thermochemical Cycle
The selection of the Cu–Cl cycle is strategic. Compared to other hydrogen production methods, this cycle is characterized by:
*   **Lower Operating Temperatures:** Making it more compatible with existing reactor technologies.
*   **Higher Thermodynamic Efficiency:** Ensuring better energy conversion rates.
*   **Environmental Impact:** It offers a pathway for large-scale hydrogen production that is entirely carbon-free, eliminating the greenhouse gas emissions associated with conventional steam methane reforming.

### 4. Strategic Importance of the Fast Breeder Programme
The facility leverages the unique capabilities of the FBTR, which has been operational for over four decades. The expertise gained through the FBTR is not only pivotal for this hydrogen project but also serves as the foundation for:
*   Validation of fuels, materials, and sodium technologies.
*   The development of the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), which is the flagship of the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme.

---

## Institutional Roles and Facility Overview

| Feature | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Technology Type** | Copper–Chlorine (Cu–Cl) Thermochemical Cycle |
| **Heat Source** | Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) |
| **Primary Developer** | Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) |
| **Operational Site** | Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), Kalpakkam |
| **Purpose** | Technology Demonstrator / Validation of nuclear-assisted hydrogen production |
| **Strategic Goal** | Energy security, decarbonization, and "AtmaNirbhar Bharat" |

---

## Key Quotes and Contextual Significance

### Dr. Ajit Kumar Mohanty, Secretary, DAE & Chairman, AEC
> "The integration of nuclear energy with emerging clean energy technologies such as hydrogen production represents a strategic pathway towards a sustainable energy future."

**Context:** Dr. Mohanty’s remarks highlight the strategic pivot of the DAE toward multi-purpose nuclear utility. He emphasizes that nuclear power's ability to provide both reliable electricity and high-temperature heat makes it the ideal partner for the global transition to hydrogen.

### Shri Sreekumar G. Pillai, Director, IGCAR
> "This achievement builds upon more than four decades of operational experience and technological excellence gained through the Fast Breeder Test Reactor programme at IGCAR."

**Context:** Shri Pillai connects this new breakthrough to the historical expertise of IGCAR. His statement underscores that the hydrogen facility is not an isolated experiment but a culmination of long-term research in reactor physics, sodium technology, and high-temperature engineering.

---

## Future Implications and Actionable Insights

The commissioning of this facility provides a roadmap for the future of nuclear-assisted hydrogen in India:

*   **Operational Optimization:** The plant will serve as a site for gathering long-term operational experience to refine the Cu–Cl process.
*   **Scalability Research:** Data from this demonstrator will support future research aimed at scaling up the technology for commercial-grade deployment.
*   **Industrial Decarbonization:** Success here opens the door for integrating nuclear reactors directly with industrial complexes requiring massive amounts of hydrogen (e.g., fertilizers, steel, and refineries).
*   **Technological Self-Reliance:** By relying on indigenous BARC technology and IGCAR engineering, the project reinforces the "AtmaNirbhar Bharat" initiative, reducing dependence on foreign intellectual property for clean energy solutions.
*   **Global Leadership:** As the world's first such facility, it establishes a global benchmark for the use of fast breeder reactors in thermochemical hydrogen production, potentially positioning India as an exporter of advanced nuclear-hydrogen expertise.

Introduction:
India's Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) has inaugurated the world's first Copper-Chlorine (Cu-Cl) thermochemical hydrogen production facility, utilizing nuclear process heat from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR). This pioneering achievement, developed indigenously by BARC and IGCAR, represents a crucial step towards large-scale, carbon-free hydrogen production and expands the role of nuclear energy beyond electricity generation.

Strategic Importance for India's Energy Security:
1. Diversification of Energy Sources: Reduces over-reliance on fossil fuels, enhancing energy independence.
2. Future Energy Carrier: Positions hydrogen as a key component of India's future energy mix, crucial for sectors difficult to electrify.
3. Reliable and Continuous Supply: Nuclear heat provides a stable and continuous energy source for hydrogen production, unlike intermittent renewables.
4. Reduced Imports: Decreases dependence on imported fossil fuels, saving foreign exchange and bolstering economic stability.

Climate Change Mitigation Efforts:
1. Carbon-Free Production: The Cu-Cl thermochemical cycle, powered by nuclear heat, produces hydrogen without generating greenhouse gas emissions.
2. Decarbonization Goals: Directly contributes to India's ambitious decarbonization targets and commitment to achieving net-zero emissions.
3. Clean Energy Transition: Accelerates the shift towards a clean and sustainable energy system by providing a green alternative to conventional hydrogen production methods (e.g., steam methane reforming).

Advancement of India's Three-Stage Nuclear Programme:

Conclusion:
The inauguration of this facility is a testament to India's leadership in advanced nuclear technologies and its strategic vision for a sustainable energy future. title: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu launches first ‘Easy Connect’ flight from Varanasi
content:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu launches first  ‘Easy Connect’ flight from Varanasi

Plans afoot to start more Hub-and-Spoke International Aviation Operations from other Tier-II & Tier-III city airports

Posted On:
                26 JUN 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant milestone towards realising the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu on June 25, 2026 launched India's first ‘Easy Connect’ flight under the Hub-and-Spoke model from Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport at Varanasi. It signifies Government's efforts to transform India into a global aviation hub and provide seamless international connectivity to passengers from Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

The Hub-and-Spoke strategy aims at making India the aviation hub of choice for Indian passengers by 2030 and for the world by 2047. The benefits extend beyond aviation. Improved international connectivity is expected to facilitate trade, tourism, investment and regional economic development. Studies undertaken by the Ministry indicate that aviation hub development could generate approximately 0.4 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute an additional USD 30 billion to India's GDP by 2030. By 2047, the cumulative impact could support approximately 16 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute nearly USD 1.4 trillion to the economy.

Speaking on the occasion, Civil Aviation Minister Shri Ram Mohan Naidu said:

"Today we take a major step forward towards realising our vision of making air travel more accessible and building a future-ready, self-reliant Indian aviation industry that is efficient, inclusive, and globally competitive.”

The Minister informed the gathering by saying, “Our new hub-and-spoke model paves the way for a monumental shift in how our citizens travel—regardless of the city one lives in India, one can begin their international journey from their home city and travel across the globe with ease and confidence, on India’s own wings."

Marking the commencement of operations, the Minister presented a commemorative boarding pass to the first few passengers to check in for the inaugural ‘Easy Connect’ flight.

The event was attended by Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Puneet Kansal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Vipin Kumar, Chairman, Airports Authority of India; Shri Campbell Wilson, Chief Executive Officer & Managing Director, Air India and other senior officials of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India, Directorate General of Civil Aviation and the airline operator.

Under the Hub-and-Spoke model, international passengers complete check-in, immigration and customs formalities at the spoke airport itself, making it the first point of departure for their international journey. For instance, passengers commencing their journey from Varanasi complete all departure formalities at Varanasi before boarding a flight to a designated Indian hub airport such as Delhi.

To ensure the highest standards of security and operational integrity, several safeguards have been incorporated into the model. Both legs of Domestic–International operations are designated as international operations. Separate physical boarding cards bearing appropriate identifiers for domestic (D) and international (I) passengers are issued to prevent passenger intermixing. International passengers travelling under the Hub-and-Spoke framework do not have access to customs declaration facilities at hub airports.

The launch of Hub-and-Spoke international operations from Varanasi marks a major advancement in India's aviation ecosystem and reinforces the Government's commitment to providing inclusive, efficient and globally competitive air connectivity for citizens across the country.
