title: English rendering of PM’s address in the 135th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 28.06.2026
content:
Prime Minister's Office

English rendering of PM’s address in the 135th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 28.06.2026

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUN 2026 11:41AM by PIB Delhi

My dear countrymen, Namaskar!

It gives me immense joy to connect with all of you once again through ‘Mann Ki Baat’. Half of the year 2026 is drawing to a close. Over these six months, we have discussed numerous achievements of our countrymen in Mann Ki Baat. In June as well, the nation has attained certain achievements that fill every citizen with pride. These successes are linked to the country's security and self-reliance. Recently, I had the opportunity to attend a Navy-related event in Kolkata. There, INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak, and INS Agray were inducted into the Indian Navy's fleet. Everything - from the design to the manufacturing of these ships - is indigenous.

Friends,

The country also achieved a major success in the aviation sector in the month of June itself. The C-295 aircraft is ‘Made in India’; C-295 aircraft has completed its maiden flight and 40 such aircrafts are being manufactured right here in India. This is providing new momentum to the MSME and aerospace sectors, raising employment opportunities, and strengthening the resolve for an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

This month, the DRDO also successfully tested an indigenous ‘Long-Range Land-Attack Cruise Missile’. It was developed jointly by DRDO laboratories and Indian industry partners; in other words, from the seas to the skies, our India is becoming increasingly secure and self-reliant.

Friends,

Another event took place in June that saw the entire world join hands with India’s efforts – and that event was ‘International Yoga Day’. This time, diverse Yoga events were held at over 2,500 locations across the globe. In our country, crores of people participated in Yoga programmes at numerous places. There has also been much discussion this month about the ‘World Yogasana Championship’ held in Ahmedabad. India won a total of 114 medals in this event, including 102 gold medals. India topped the medal tally at this championship. I extend my heartiest congratulations to all the winning athletes.

Friends,

The people are the soul of any nation. And when the people of that country make a resolve, no force can deter them from their goal. This power of public participation in nation-building is a tremendous asset for India, and we are experiencing this public participation time and again.

Friends,

In view of the prevalent war-like situation in West Asia, I had urged countrymen on a few points. I had asked people to avoid buying gold for some time, as far as possible. I urged people to avoid holidaying abroad and encouraged carpooling. I also requested farmers to adopt chemical-free farming, protect their farmlands, and maximize the use of natural fertilizers. Friends, I am grateful to every citizen of the country; not only have they supported my appeal, they are also actively cooperating in every way. Many families have shared their experiences with me through messages. Numerous families have decided not to buy gold for weddings in their homes this time; if the need arises, they would recycle old gold to create new jewellery. Many people have also written on social media about how they have postponed their foreign trips, this time.

Friends,

People have shared many experiences regarding carpooling as well. Those who used to travel in their own vehicles in the same direction every day have now started commuting together. People are making every effort to use buses and the metro, which is resulting in savings on petrol and diesel. Similarly, reports are coming in about the increased consumption of natural fertilizers in various parts of the country. Friends, I am happy that we Indians are facing this global crisis together. I am confident that this very power of public participation will strengthen us and lead us to success.

My dear countrymen,

In our country, occasions like birthdays, weddings, and family functions are not merely private affairs but celebrations for the entire community. Every family wishes to share its joy with others, and people often give gifts to their guests. Friends, a family in Nanded, Maharashtra, has done something to share their happiness that has become a topic of discussion. The Pethkar family resides in the village of Bahadurpura in Nanded. This family felt that if they were to share their joy, they should offer something that could serve as a support system for a family during difficult times. On the occasion of a wedding in their home, the family arranged accident insurance for approximately 3,500 villagers. Each individual was provided with an insurance cover of one lakh rupees. The sentiment behind this initiative is truly touching. The family had observed that households often face severe financial hardship following an accident. During such times, even a little aid turns out to be of great support.

Friends,

The government is extending this protective shield to crores of families across the country. Under the ‘Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana’ for an annual premium of just ₹20 - meaning a premium of only ₹20 for the entire year - one gets 'accidental insurance' cover of up to ₹2 lakh. So far, more than 58 crore people have joined this scheme.

Among them, approximately 28 crore are women - our mothers, sisters, and daughters. Affected families have received assistance amounting to over ₹3,700 crore through this scheme to date, as per the accounts available so far.

Friends,

Similarly, the 'Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana' is equally important. This scheme provides an insurance cover of ₹2 lakh to a person's family in the event of their unfortunate death. Its annual premium is just ₹436 - which works out to barely ₹1.50 per day. More than 27 crore people have joined this scheme so far. Under it, around 11 lakh families across the country have received assistance totalling approximately ₹22,000 crore. These figures are massive. Behind these numbers lie the individual stories of lakhs of families; somewhere, a mother received help to continue her children's education, while elsewhere, a wife found the support needed to manage household responsibilities.

Friends,

Often, a significant safety net can begin with a very small amount and a tiny step; even a small decision can bring about a major change. I urge all of you to share information about these schemes with your families.

My dear countrymen,

In 'Mann Ki Baat', let us now discuss a subject that is thousands of years old - one that has been deeply ingrained in human society for millennia. That subject is superstition. Superstition is often not merely a misconception; it begets fear, and when fear dominates the mind, a person stops seeing the truth. People steeped in superstition begin making decisions without logic or knowledge of the facts—decisions that lead to great harm. At the same time, there are those in society who challenge such beliefs based on science, experience, and logic. The journey from superstition to faith is not easy, and today I certainly want to tell you about one such successful journey.

Friends,

A bird is found in Assam known as the ‘Hargila’. The ‘Hargila’ is a rare bird. It plays a vital role in keeping nature clean. However, for a long time, it was considered inauspicious in certain parts of Assam. People disliked seeing it in their vicinity. Often, trees housing ‘Hargila’ nests were even cut down. Just imagine—a bird that helps clean the environment became a victim of people's fears. It was during that time that biologist Purnima Devi Barman witnessed it all. She resolved to change the misconceptions deeply rooted in people's minds. She spoke to women and explained the facts based on science; gradually, women began joining this campaign.

Then, a major transformation began. The bird that was once driven away as a bad omen started becoming the identity of the villages. Thousands of rural women stepped forward to save the ‘Hargila’—today, they are known as the ‘Hargila Army’. These women also had to contend with societal resistance. They worked day and night to convince society and ultimately succeeded in leaving superstition behind. They have demonstrated that when the right information is conveyed, even age-old mindsets can change.

Friends,

I often say: "Those who play, blossom." Today, the number of young people in the country who are both playing sports and blossoming is growing rapidly. Compared to the past, far more young people are now pursuing sports as a career. I have learned about two such initiatives in Nagaland that are quite interesting. The first initiative is the ‘Nagaland Baby League’. Hearing the name, you might presume this is just an ordinary league for very young children, but that is not the case. It is an extraordinary league for children aged 5 to 10 to 12 - blossoming youngsters - that not only inspires them and nurtures their speed and talent but also helps establish their identity. It was launched to connect as many children as possible in Nagaland with football. Boys and girls aged five to twelve can participate. The league has now completed three years of operation. This league has had a positive impact on the children.

Friends,

Another commendable initiative is underway in Nagaland: the ‘Nagaland Women Futsal League’. ‘Futsal’ might be a new term for some of you; let me explain that it is also known as indoor football. In each team, there are only five players, and the playing court is much smaller than a standard football field. Consequently, players must make quick decisions and effectively utilize their technique and skills. The Nagaland Women Futsal League is providing a wonderful platform for our daughters to showcase their talent. I commend the people of Nagaland for such initiatives; these efforts serve as an inspiration to other parts of the country as well.

Friends,

This is the age of technology. New research is taking place every day. Ever new AI innovations are coming up. In such times, a crucial question arises: how can we preserve people's creativity? How do we remain connected to our roots while advancing with new technology? Nalanda University has found a solution to these questions. Our Nalanda University—dating back thousands of years—is now shaping India's destiny in a new avatar. Two years ago, I had the opportunity to dedicate to the people the new campus of Nalanda University. Nalanda University has revived our ancient tradition of *Shaastraarth* i.e. intellectual discourse.

*Shaastraarth* is not merely a medium for expressing one's views; it is a disciplined process of dialogue, debate, and deep contemplation. It requires articulating one's position backed by logic and facts - areas demanding mastery. This process also teaches us to listen to and understand the views of others with patience. I am pleased that Nalanda University has incorporated this into its convocation ceremony. Nearly half of the participating students came from other countries. This effort to bridge an ancient tradition with contemporary times is highly commendable. I extend my heartiest congratulations to Nalanda University for this initiative. I would also urge other universities across the country to consider similar initiatives.

Friends,

Another significant effort is underway to prepare the youth for new technology while keeping them rooted in their heritage. The Central Sanskrit University in Delhi is launching a B.Tech program in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. This marks a crucial step towards integrating modern technology with India's traditional knowledge. It will facilitate the development of new AI tools for Indian languages ​​and accelerate the digitization and preservation of our ancient texts and manuscripts. I convey my best wishes to the Central Sanskrit University for this endeavour.

Friends,

Indian culture is reaching various corners of the globe today. People across the world are discovering and embracing our songs, music, and spirituality. Thousands of kilometers away from India, in the Caribbean Sea, lies a country called the Dominican Republic. The Indian population there is around 100—perhaps even fewer. Despite this, a wonderful initiative connected to Indian culture and spirituality is underway there. A team has been formed by some Spanish-speaking locals; this team is named 'Brahmakamal Dominicana.' The members study Vedic literature together and are learning to chant Vedic mantras. They have received no formal training on this; but they have learnt the correct pronunciation by listening to audio recordings.

Today, they chant several mantras—such as the Purusha Suktam, Sri Suktam, Sri Rudram, Durga Suktam, and Devi Mahatmyam—with great proficiency. Their effort to learn our traditions while living so far from India is truly inspiring. I extend my best wishes to all the members of 'Brahmakamal Dominicana' for their endeavors. I wholeheartedly appreciate all those who are making continuous efforts to popularize Indian culture worldwide.

My dear countrymen,

Meghalaya is known for its clouds and breathtaking landscapes. Anyone who visits Meghalaya also cherishes the memory of the warmth and sense of belonging offered by its people even long after they leave.

However, there is another unique feature of Meghalaya that I wish to discuss with you today in ‘Mann Ki Baat’, that is Meghalaya’s root bridges. I am referring to bridges made of roots, not the kind of route one travels on. The story behind these root bridges is fascinating. These bridges are not built in a matter of days or years; it takes decades for them to take shape. The roots of rubber trees are gradually guided in specific directions and trained to span across water streams.

Over time, these roots transform into sturdy bridges. These bridges possess another unique quality: they are living bridges. They grow stronger with the passage of time. They reflect the creativity of the people of Meghalaya. These embody years of patience and a deep respect for nature. These bridges demonstrate the amazing things humans can create in harmony with nature. They are a heritage of our country and our land. India has now applied to have Meghalaya’s root bridges included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site Network.

Friends,

climate change poses several challenges to these root bridges. Amidst this, the people of Meghalaya have admirably shouldered the responsibility of preserving this natural heritage. Previously, it was not even easy to determine exactly how many such bridges existed; the local people themselves took the initiative to count them.

Subsequently, the communities also took up the responsibility of maintaining these bridges. Today, local residents look after more than 120 root bridges. Some teams inspect the condition of these bridges annually, and some individuals have even established nurseries to strengthen the surrounding areas. An entire ecosystem has thus developed around their conservation. You may have noticed that Hally War ji was honored with a Padma Award this year; he has dedicated over 50 years of his life to the care of these root bridges. His dedication is an inspiration to us all. Friends, if you have ever visited these root bridges, do share your photographs on social media. Your pictures will inspire others to learn about this unique heritage of Meghalaya.

My dear fellow citizens,

We all desire our village to be neat and clean and our city to look beautiful. Yet, we rarely pause to consider who clears the waste that accumulates around us. Most people presume it is someone else's responsibility—that someone else will handle the cleaning. However, there are individuals among us whose mindset serves as a great inspiration. I had the opportunity to learn about some women from Biaora in the Rajgarh district of Madhya Pradesh. They resolved to remove the plastic waste scattered around their area. Instead of contemplating for someone else to bring about change, they took the initiative to collect plastic waste and empty bottles from across the town themselves. Gradually, this effort expanded, and the collected plastic began to be converted into 'eco-bricks.'

Today, these very eco-bricks are being used to beautify public spaces. In Rajgarh, hundreds of kilograms of plastic have been recycled and put to productive use over the past few months. In other words, the plastic that once polluted the city is now contributing to its beauty, thanks to the efforts of these women. I congratulate all the sisters of Biaora and the associates involved in this initiative.

My dear fellow citizens,

Many people have written to me suggesting that I speak about a special topic. This topic relates to ‘Ganesh Utsav’. Although there is still quite some time left for ‘Ganesh Utsav’, people have urged that this subject be discussed right now. In fact, the work of crafting Ganesh idols begins well in advance; idol makers and those involved in the idol trade become active right now. Therefore, I urge all of you... please make an effort to ensure that the idol of Ganpati Bappa installed in your home, society, or neighborhood is made from the soil of our own country and crafted by the hands of our own potters and local artisans. I also urge those who make Ganesh idols to prioritize clay idols, and I ask buyers to check what the idol is made of and which country it was produced in. Do not buy idols made of Plaster of Paris at all.

Friends,

Clay idols dissolve naturally in water after the worship rituals conclude. This helps protect our rivers, ponds, and the environment. It allows us to uphold our faith while also fulfilling our responsibility towards nature. When we purchase idols from local artisans, we strengthen the resolve of being ‘Vocal for Local’. I am confident that during this ‘Ganesh Utsav’—and indeed during every such festival—we will give serious thought to these matters and take steps in the national interest.

Friends,

The greatest strength of our country lies in her people. The various efforts—big and small—taking place across the country teach us a great deal. These endeavours demonstrate that when there is determination and the support of society, significant change can be achieved. Do keep writing to me about such efforts happening in your vicinity. Continue sharing your thoughts and suggestions; a small initiative in your area could well become an inspiration for the entire nation. We shall meet again next month to discuss new endeavors undertaken by our countrymen. Until then, take care of yourselves and your families - and yes, water conservation is a must! We must save every single drop of rainwater. We cannot let the momentum of the ‘Catch the Rain’ campaign slacken in the slightest. So, I urge you specially: let us come together to save every drop of rain.

Thank you very much. Namaskar.

*****

# Briefing Document: Analysis of Mann Ki Baat Episode 135 (June 28, 2026)

## Executive Summary

The 135th episode of *Mann Ki Baat*, delivered on June 28, 2026, serves as a comprehensive review of India’s progress in the first half of the year. The address highlights significant milestones in national security and self-reliance (*Atmanirbhar Bharat*), specifically within the naval and aviation sectors. A major portion of the discourse focuses on the power of public participation (*Jan Bhagidari*) as a tool for overcoming global economic crises and social challenges. The document also emphasizes the integration of ancient Indian traditions with modern technology, the global expansion of Indian culture, and the critical importance of environmental conservation through indigenous practices and community-led initiatives.

---

## Detailed Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. National Security and Indigenous Manufacturing
The month of June 2026 marked significant advancements in India’s defense capabilities, characterized by a shift toward domestic production.

| Sector | Achievement | Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Naval Power** | Induction of INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak, and INS Agray | All ships were indigenously designed and manufactured in Kolkata. |
| **Aviation** | C-295 Aircraft | The "Made in India" C-295 completed its maiden flight; 40 units are being manufactured domestically, boosting the MSME and aerospace sectors. |
| **Missile Tech** | Long-Range Land-Attack Cruise Missile | Successfully tested by DRDO in collaboration with Indian industry partners. |

### 2. Public Participation and Economic Resilience
In response to the volatile situation in West Asia, the Indian public has demonstrated collective resilience by adhering to government advisories aimed at stabilizing the economy and reducing resource consumption.

*   **Economic Measures:** Citizens have reportedly reduced gold purchases, opted to recycle old jewelry for weddings, and postponed foreign travel.
*   **Resource Conservation:** There is a notable shift toward carpooling and the use of public transport (buses and metro) to save on fuel.
*   **Agricultural Shift:** Farmers are increasingly adopting chemical-free farming and natural fertilizers to protect land health.

### 3. Social Security and Grassroots Welfare
The address underscores the importance of the government's "protective shield" through low-cost insurance schemes, highlighting their impact on millions of families.

*   **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana:** Offers ₹2 lakh accidental insurance for a ₹20 annual premium. Over 58 crore people (including 28 crore women) are enrolled, with ₹3,700 crore in assistance distributed.
*   **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana:** Provides ₹2 lakh life insurance for a ₹436 annual premium (approx. ₹1.50 per day). Over 27 crore people are enrolled, with ₹22,000 crore in claims paid to 11 lakh families.
*   **Community Initiative:** The Pethkar family in Nanded, Maharashtra, exemplified social responsibility by providing accident insurance to 3,500 villagers on the occasion of a family wedding.

### 4. Cultural Heritage and Modern Integration
A central theme is the revitalization of ancient knowledge systems and their application in the modern technological era.

*   **Nalanda University:** The university has revived the tradition of *Shaastraarth* (intellectual discourse), integrating logic and debate into contemporary education.
*   **Technological Fusion:** Central Sanskrit University in Delhi is launching a B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science to digitize ancient texts and develop AI tools for Indian languages.
*   **Global Reach:** The 'Brahmakamal Dominicana' group in the Dominican Republic exemplifies the global spread of Indian spirituality, with locals learning to chant Vedic mantras with high proficiency.

### 5. Environmental Stewardship
The document outlines several community-driven environmental success stories and conservation efforts:

*   **Hargila Army (Assam):** Led by biologist Purnima Devi Barman, rural women overcame superstitions surrounding the "inauspicious" Hargila bird to protect the species and the environment.
*   **Living Root Bridges (Meghalaya):** These bridges, grown from rubber tree roots over decades, represent a harmonious relationship with nature. India has applied for their inclusion as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
*   **Eco-Bricks (Madhya Pradesh):** Women in Biaora are collecting plastic waste and bottles to create "eco-bricks" for beautifying public spaces.

---

## Important Quotes and Context

> **"Everything - from the design to the manufacturing of these ships - is indigenous."**
*   **Context:** Discussing the induction of three new ships into the Indian Navy in Kolkata, emphasizing the success of domestic defense manufacturing.

> **"The journey from superstition to faith is not easy... when fear dominates the mind, a person stops seeing the truth."**
*   **Context:** Relating the story of the Hargila bird in Assam, where conservation efforts had to first overcome deep-seated local superstitions.

> **"Often, a significant safety net can begin with a very small amount and a tiny step; even a small decision can bring about a major change."**
*   **Context:** Urging citizens to enroll in and share information about the government's low-cost insurance schemes (PMSBY and PMJJBY).

> **"Shaastraarth is not merely a medium for expressing one's views; it is a disciplined process of dialogue, debate, and deep contemplation."**
*   **Context:** Highlighting the academic traditions being revived at the new Nalanda University campus.

---

## Actionable Insights and Directives

1.  **Support Local Artisans for Festivals:** For the upcoming *Ganesh Utsav*, citizens are urged to purchase idols made of local clay rather than Plaster of Paris. This supports local potters ("Vocal for Local") and protects water bodies.
2.  **Enroll in Social Security:** Families are encouraged to utilize the *Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana* and *Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana* to secure their financial future at a minimal cost.
3.  **Water Conservation:** As a critical priority, every citizen is directed to maximize rainwater harvesting under the 'Catch the Rain' campaign to combat climate challenges.
4.  **Promote Sports at the Grassroots:** Regional bodies are encouraged to look toward Nagaland’s "Baby League" (football for ages 5-12) and "Women’s Futsal League" as models for nurturing talent and technique in children and women.
5.  **Fact-Based Decision Making:** Using the example of the Hargila Army, the document encourages the use of science and logic to challenge and overcome social superstitions that harm the environment or society.

mains_questions.question: The recent induction of indigenously designed and manufactured naval ships and aircraft highlights India's commitment to 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' in the defense sector. Discuss the strategic and economic implications of defense indigenization for India, particularly focusing on its impact on the MSME sector and employment generation. (150 words, 10 marks)
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** India's push for 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (self-reliant India) in defense aims to reduce import dependence and bolster national security through indigenous design, development, and manufacturing of defense equipment. Recent inductions like INS Dunagiri and C-295 aircraft exemplify this commitment.

**Strategic Implications:**
*   **Enhanced National Security:** Reduces vulnerability to external supply disruptions during conflicts.
*   **Strategic Autonomy:** Frees India from geopolitical pressures associated with foreign military hardware.
*   **Technological Sovereignty:** Fosters domestic R&D and innovation, leading to cutting-edge defense technologies.

**Economic Implications:**
*   **Boost to MSME Sector:** Creates a robust ecosystem for small and medium enterprises to supply components, sub-systems, and services to larger defense manufacturers. This diversifies the industrial base.
*   **Employment Generation:** Direct employment in defense public sector undertakings, private defense firms, and MSMEs, along with indirect jobs in allied sectors like logistics, maintenance, and R&D.
*   **Foreign Exchange Savings:** Reduces the outflow of currency spent on defense imports.
*   **Skill Development:** Promotes specialized skills in engineering, advanced manufacturing, and defense technology.
*   **Export Potential:** Positions India as a potential exporter of defense equipment, contributing to economic growth.

**Conclusion:** Defense indigenization is a strategic imperative that not only strengthens India's security apparatus but also acts as a significant catalyst for economic growth, fostering a vibrant domestic industrial base and creating substantial employment opportunities.

mains_questions.question: Public participation is often hailed as a critical component of effective governance and national resilience. In the context of the Prime Minister's recent appeals for citizen cooperation in addressing economic and environmental challenges, critically examine the significance of public participation and suggest measures to further enhance it in India. (250 words, 15 marks)
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** Public participation, the active involvement of citizens in decision-making and implementation processes, is vital for a robust democracy and national resilience. The Prime Minister's recent appeals regarding economic prudence (e.g., avoiding gold, carpooling) and environmental responsibility (e.g., chemical-free farming) underscore its importance in navigating contemporary challenges.

**Significance of Public Participation:**
*   **Strengthening National Resilience:** Collective action by citizens can mitigate economic shocks (e.g., saving foreign exchange, reducing fuel consumption) and promote environmental sustainability.
*   **Effective Policy Implementation:** Citizen buy-in and cooperation ensure better ground-level implementation and success of government initiatives.
*   **Resource Mobilization:** Encourages optimal utilization of domestic resources and reduces reliance on external factors.

On June 28, 2026, the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, issued a formal tribute to celebrate the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Shri PV Narasimha Rao. The communication, released through the Prime Minister's Office and official social media channels, highlights Rao’s legacy as a pivotal figure in India’s developmental trajectory. The tribute characterizes Rao as an "able administrator" and a "distinguished scholar" who provided essential leadership during a transformative period in the nation's history.

The tributes paid to Shri PV Narasimha Rao focus on three primary dimensions of his legacy: historical impact, administrative capability, and intellectual depth.

### 1. Leadership During Critical Transitions
The Prime Minister emphasized that Rao’s tenure occurred during a "critical phase" of India's history. The tribute acknowledges that during this period, Rao made "enduring contributions" that were foundational to the nation's progress. This framing suggests that his leadership was not merely routine but was essential for navigating significant national challenges.

### 2. Administrative Excellence
Rao is specifically recognized for his professional governance skills. The Prime Minister noted that Rao "made a mark as an able administrator," signifying a legacy of effective management and institutional oversight.

### 3. Intellectual and Cultural Scholarship
Beyond his political and administrative roles, the tribute highlights Rao’s personal attributes as a thinker. He is described as:

*   **Culturally Literate:** Blessed with an "immense knowledge and understanding" of the diverse cultural fabric of India.

| **Context of Leadership** | Served during a "critical phase" of history |
| **Professional Identity** | Able administrator |

---

The following statements were issued by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 28, 2026:

## Actionable Insights and Perspectives

The tribute provides a framework for how the current administration views the legacy of Shri PV Narasimha Rao. These insights reflect the values prioritized in national leadership:

mains_questions.question: The economic reforms of 1991, often attributed to the P.V. Narasimha Rao government, are considered a turning point in India's economic trajectory. Discuss the key features of these reforms and critically evaluate their long-term impact on the Indian economy.
mains_questions.answer:
## Introduction
*   Briefly introduce the economic crisis of 1991 and the necessity for reforms.
*   Mention P.V. Narasimha Rao's role as Prime Minister and Dr. Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister in initiating these reforms.

## Key Features of the 1991 Reforms
*   **Liberalization:** Dismantling the 'License Raj', industrial deregulation, abolition of MRTP Act.
*   **Privatization:** Disinvestment in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
*   **Globalization:** Opening up the economy to foreign direct investment (FDI) and foreign institutional investment (FII), reduction in customs duties, partial convertibility of the Rupee.
*   **Fiscal Reforms:** Efforts to reduce fiscal deficit, tax reforms (e.g., introduction of VAT later).
*   **Financial Sector Reforms:** Deregulation of interest rates, strengthening of banking sector.

## Long-term Impact on the Indian Economy
### Positive Impacts:
*   **Higher Economic Growth:** Shift to a higher growth trajectory.
*   **Increased Foreign Investment:** Inflow of FDI and FII, boosting capital formation.
*   **Rise of the Service Sector:** India emerged as a global hub for IT and IT-enabled services.
*   **Poverty Reduction:** Significant decline in poverty rates over the subsequent decades.
*   **Increased Competition and Efficiency:** Improved productivity and consumer choice.
*   **Integration with Global Economy:** Enhanced trade and diplomatic ties.

### Critical Evaluation/Challenges:
*   **Increased Inequality:** Widening gap between rich and poor, urban and rural areas.
*   **Regional Disparities:** Uneven development across states.
*   **Impact on Agriculture:** Limited reforms in the agricultural sector, leading to distress.
*   **Environmental Concerns:** Increased industrialization leading to environmental degradation.
*   **Financial Sector Vulnerabilities:** Exposure to global financial shocks.
*   **Jobless Growth:** Concerns about the ability of the economy to create sufficient jobs for the growing workforce.

## Conclusion
*   Summarize that the 1991 reforms were transformative, pulling India out of a crisis and setting it on a path of sustained growth.
*   Acknowledge the need for continuous reforms to address the lingering challenges of inequality, agricultural distress, and inclusive growth.

mains_questions.question: The President of India, as the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, confers various awards for distinguished service. Discuss the constitutional provisions empowering the President in this role and analyze the significance of such awards in enhancing the morale and operational effectiveness of the Indian Armed Forces.
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:**
The President of India, as the ceremonial head of the state and the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces, plays a pivotal role in recognizing the valor and distinguished service of military personnel through various awards. This act not only upholds constitutional principles but also significantly impacts the morale and operational readiness of the forces.

**Constitutional Provisions Empowering the President:**
*   **Article 53(2):** Explicitly states that the supreme command of the Defence Forces of the Union shall be vested in the President and the exercise thereof shall be regulated by law.
*   **Article 74:** The President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, ensuring civilian control over the military.
*   **Article 77:** All executive action of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.
*   **Role in Appointments:** The President appoints the Chiefs of Staff of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
*   **Declaration of War and Peace:** While exercised on the advice of the Cabinet, the formal declaration is made in the President's name.
*   **Conferring Honours:** The President is the source of all honours and awards, including those for distinguished service in the armed forces.

**Significance of Awards in Enhancing Morale and Operational Effectiveness:**
*   **Recognition and Motivation:** Awards like Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM), Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM), and Uttam Yudh Seva Medal (UYSM) acknowledge exceptional service, bravery, and leadership, serving as a powerful motivator.
*   **Boosting Morale:** Public recognition by the Supreme Commander instills a sense of pride, honour, and belonging among personnel and their families.
*   **Fostering Professionalism:** These awards encourage high standards of duty, discipline, and dedication, promoting a culture of excellence.
*   **Inspiring Future Generations:** Awardees become role models, inspiring younger personnel to strive for similar achievements and uphold the ethos of the armed forces.
*   **Strengthening National Security:** A highly motivated and recognized force is more effective in defending national interests and maintaining peace and security.
*   **Public Trust and Respect:** The ceremonies enhance public awareness and appreciation for the sacrifices and contributions of the armed forces, strengthening the civil-military relationship.

**Conclusion:**
The President's role in conferring distinguished service awards is a crucial constitutional function that goes beyond mere ceremony. It is a vital mechanism for reinforcing the values of courage, sacrifice, and dedication within the Indian Armed Forces, thereby directly contributing to their morale, operational effectiveness, and ultimately, national security.

**Introduction:**
The Indian Armed Forces recognize the exceptional contributions of their personnel through a structured system of distinguished service awards. These accolades, presented by the President of India, are crucial for acknowledging selfless service and promoting high standards within the military.

**Categories of Distinguished Service Awards:**
The PIB release mentions Ati Vishisht Seva Medals, Uttam Yudh Seva Medals, Param Vishisht Seva Medals, and Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medals. Generally, distinguished service awards are categorized based on the degree of service:

*   **Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM):** Awarded for distinguished service of an exceptional order. It is the highest peacetime distinguished service decoration.
*   **Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal (SYSM):** Awarded for distinguished service of an exceptional order during wartime. (Though the PIB lists it under 'Distinguished Service Awards' in a peacetime context, it's primarily a wartime award).
*   **Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM):** Awarded for distinguished service of an exceptional order. It is the second-highest peacetime distinguished service decoration.
*   **Uttam Yudh Seva Medal (UYSM):** Awarded for distinguished service of an exceptional order during wartime.
*   **Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM):** Awarded for distinguished service of a high order.
*   **Yudh Seva Medal (YSM):** Awarded for distinguished service during wartime.

These awards recognize leadership, administrative acumen, strategic planning, and overall contribution to the armed forces, distinct from gallantry awards which recognize acts of bravery in combat.

**Impact on Fostering a Culture of Excellence and Dedication:**
*   **Motivation and Recognition:** Awards provide tangible recognition for years of dedicated service, often under challenging conditions, motivating personnel to excel.
*   **Setting Benchmarks:** They establish high standards of performance and conduct, encouraging others to emulate the awardees' commitment and professionalism.
*   **Leadership Development:** Many distinguished service awards recognize effective leadership and administrative capabilities, promoting these qualities within the officer corps.
*   **Morale Booster:** The public acknowledgment of service by the highest office boosts the morale of the entire force, reinforcing their sense of purpose and value.
*   **Preserving Military Ethos:** These awards help in preserving and promoting the core values of the armed forces such as duty, honour, integrity, and selfless service.
*   **Public Image:** They enhance the public's perception and respect for the armed forces, highlighting their professionalism and dedication to national service.

**Critical Assessment:**
While highly impactful, the system can face challenges:
*   **Subjectivity:** The selection process, though rigorous, can sometimes be perceived as subjective.
*   **Visibility:** Ensuring that deserving personnel from all ranks and branches receive due consideration is crucial.
*   **Balancing Individual vs. Team Effort:** While awards recognize individuals, the military operates on teamwork, and striking a balance is important.

**Conclusion:**
Distinguished service awards are more than just medals; they are powerful instruments for cultivating a culture of excellence, dedication, and professionalism within the Indian Armed Forces. By recognizing exemplary service, they inspire current and future generations of military personnel to uphold the highest standards in safeguarding the nation.

mains_questions.question: The establishment of Central Tribal Universities signifies a focused approach towards inclusive education. mains_questions.answer:
Introduction:
Briefly introduce Central Tribal Universities and their specific objective of catering to tribal communities.

Importance in Empowering Tribal Communities:
- Providing equitable access to higher education for historically marginalized tribal groups.
- Preserving, promoting, and researching tribal languages, cultures, arts, and traditions.
- Developing skills and knowledge relevant to the specific needs and resources of tribal areas.
- Addressing educational disparities and bridging the gap between tribal and non-tribal populations.
- Fostering leadership and intellectual capital within tribal communities.

Constitutional Provisions for Tribal Education:
- Article 46: Directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, especially the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
- Article 15(4): Enables the State to make any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
- Article 29: Protects the interests of minorities, including their right to conserve their distinct language, script, or culture, which implicitly supports culturally relevant education.
- Fifth and Sixth Schedules: Provide for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas, respectively, influencing educational policies and institutions in these regions.

Government Initiatives for Promoting Tribal Education:
- Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): Residential schools for tribal students to provide quality education from Class VI to XII.
- Scholarship Schemes: Post-Matric Scholarship for ST students, National Overseas Scholarship Scheme, and various other financial aid programs.
- Grants to States: Financial assistance to State Governments for tribal development, including educational infrastructure and programs.
- Vocational Training Programs: Initiatives to impart job-oriented skills to tribal youth.
- Role of Ministry of Tribal Affairs: Nodal ministry for the overall policy, planning, and coordination of programs for the development of Scheduled Tribes, including education.

Conclusion:
Reiterate the critical role of Central Tribal Universities and the comprehensive framework of constitutional provisions and government initiatives in achieving inclusive, equitable, and culturally sensitive education for tribal communities, thereby contributing to their holistic empowerment and national development.

questions.question: In the context of the Sanskrit Subhashitam shared by the Prime Minister, what does the term 'Paravarajnah' ($परावरज्ञः$) signify regarding the character of a leader?

answerOptions.text: A person who possesses knowledge of both the profound (transcendental) and the mundane (worldly) realities.
answerOptions.rationale: The term combines 'Para' (higher/beyond) and 'Avara' (lower/immediate), indicating a leader who understands the ultimate truth as well as the practical nuances of the world.

answerOptions.text: An individual who focuses exclusively on the higher spiritual realms while ignoring worldly customs.
answerOptions.rationale: This ignores the 'Avara' aspect of the term, which refers to the immediate, worldly details that a leader must also master.

answerOptions.text: A leader who prioritizes the 'Avara' or lower-level administrative tasks over philosophical principles.
answerOptions.rationale: This overlooks the 'Para' component, which implies a grasp of higher principles and overarching truths necessary for true wisdom.

answerOptions.text: One who is only an expert in the 'Para' or external cultures while remaining ignorant of their own.
answerOptions.rationale: The term refers to the depth and hierarchy of knowledge (high and low) rather than a distinction between domestic and foreign cultures.

questions.hint: Analyze the etymology of the term, where 'Para' refers to the ultimate or distant and 'Avara' refers to the proximate or lower.

questions.question: The Subhashitam mentions 'Deshacharan' and 'Samayan' as key areas of study for one who seeks leadership. What do these terms primarily represent in the framework of governance and social harmony?

answerOptions.text: Regional customs and the specific conventions or requirements of the time.
answerOptions.rationale: 'Desha' refers to the land or region, and 'Samaya' refers to time, occasion, or established conventions, suggesting that leadership requires contextual awareness.

answerOptions.text: Strict legal codes and the geographical boundaries of a nation-state.
answerOptions.rationale: While 'Desha' relates to land, 'Achara' refers to conduct or customs rather than modern statutory law or rigid borders.

answerOptions.text: Economic trade routes and the chronological history of ancient dynasties.
answerOptions.rationale: The verse focuses on the living culture and social behavior ('Achara') rather than purely economic or historical data points.

answerOptions.text: The military protocols of a region and the religious festivals of a specific era.
answerOptions.rationale: This is too narrow; the terms encompass broader cultural and social conventions that facilitate trust across different communities.

questions.hint: Think about how 'Desha' (land) and 'Samaya' (time) relate to the behavior and practices of people in those contexts.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister's commentary on the Subhashitam, what are the primary psychological and social benefits of respecting diverse cultures?

answerOptions.text: The development of trust, cooperation, and a strengthened sense of brotherhood.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM explicitly mentions that respecting different cultures fosters 'Vishwaas' (trust), 'Sahyog' (cooperation), and 'Bhaichara' (brotherhood).

answerOptions.text: The standardisation of global traditions into a single unified cultural identity.
answerOptions.rationale: The text emphasizes respecting 'diversity' (अलग-अलग संस्कृतियों) rather than homogenizing or standardizing them into one.

answerOptions.text: The elimination of local traditions in favor of a universal set of administrative rules.
answerOptions.rationale: The Subhashitam encourages learning and respecting regional customs ('Deshacharan') rather than replacing them.

answerOptions.text: A purely economic partnership based on mutual financial gain and market stability.
answerOptions.rationale: The focus of the PM's message is on the emotional and social bonds of understanding and brotherhood, not just economic transactions.

questions.hint: Recall the specific keywords used in the Prime Minister's post regarding the feelings that grow among people.

questions.question: In the phrase 'Mahajanasya adhipatyam karoti' ($महाजनस्याधिपत्यं करोति$), what does the verse identify as the result of a leader's cultural adaptability?

answerOptions.text: Gaining leadership and authority through the respect and consensus of the great or the people.
answerOptions.rationale: 'Mahajana' refers to the collective or the great people, and 'Adhipatyam' refers to leadership or sovereignty achieved through knowledge and respect.

answerOptions.text: The acquisition of vast territorial wealth and the expansion of an empire by force.
answerOptions.rationale: The verse implies a leadership gained through knowledge ('Pavarajnah') and understanding of customs, not through military conquest.

answerOptions.text: The total isolation of the leader from the 'Mahajana' to maintain an aura of mystery.
answerOptions.rationale: The verse states the leader gains authority 'over' or 'among' them, implying deep social engagement rather than isolation.

answerOptions.text: A mandate to enforce one's own 'Jati-dharma' onto all other societies.

questions.question: Which quality is highlighted in the Subhashitam as essential for a person who 'desires to be' (Bubhushete) a leader in a diverse world?

answerOptions.text: An inquisitive desire to understand the customs, times, and traditions of various groups.
answerOptions.rationale: The verse uses 'Bubhushete' in conjunction with 'Deshacharan', 'Samayan', and 'Jatidharman', highlighting the importance of the will to learn diverse social structures.

answerOptions.text: A strict adherence to one's own regional practices to set an example for others.

answerOptions.text: The mastery of a single language to communicate with all people uniformly.

# Global Cultural Respect and Cooperation: Analysis of the Sanskrit Subhashitam shared by the Prime Minister

## Executive Summary
On June 29, 2026, the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, issued a public communication via social media and the Press Information Bureau (PIB) highlighting a traditional Sanskrit Subhashitam (wise saying). The core message of this communication emphasizes that the deliberate respect of diverse cultures, customs, and traditions is the foundational element for fostering global trust, cooperation, and brotherhood. By sharing this ancient wisdom, the Prime Minister reinforces the value of mutual understanding in strengthening social and international fabrics.

---

## Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. The Value of Cultural Diversity and Recognition
The provided text centers on the importance of acknowledging "Deshacharan" (regional customs) and the diverse practices of different groups. The primary theme is that cultural diversity should not merely be observed but actively respected. The document suggests that such respect is a prerequisite for any meaningful engagement between different sets of people.

### 2. Social Cohesion and Brotherhood
A significant portion of the Prime Minister’s commentary focuses on the outcomes of cultural respect. The analysis identifies three specific results:
*   **Trust:** Respect acts as a catalyst for building confidence between different communities.
*   **Cooperation:** Once trust is established, a spirit of collaboration naturally follows.
*   **Brotherhood:** The ultimate goal is the strengthening of mutual understanding and the creation of a sense of brotherhood that transcends cultural boundaries.

### 3. The Path to Leadership and Influence
The Sanskrit verse provides a deeper insight into the characteristics of a leader (Mahajana). It suggests that an individual who possesses the wisdom to understand both the high and the low (or the near and the far) and who honors the laws and customs of various lands and peoples, naturally ascends to a position of leadership and command. Influence, therefore, is rooted in the empathetic understanding of others' traditions.

---

## Important Quotes and Contextual Analysis

| Quote (Source Context) | Language/Origin | Contextual Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| “देशाचारान् समयाञ्जातिधर्मान् बुभूषते यस्तु परावरज्ञः। स तत्र तत्राधिगतः सदैव महाजनस्याधिपत्यं करोति॥” | Sanskrit Subhashitam | The foundational verse which argues that he who respects regional customs and the duties of various groups gains leadership among the people. |
| "दुनिया की अलग-अलग संस्कृतियों का सम्मान करने से लोगों के बीच विश्वास और सहयोग की भावना बढ़ती है।" | Hindi (PM’s commentary) | Directly links the act of respecting global cultures to the practical benefits of increased trust and cooperation. |
| "इससे आपसी समझ और भाईचारा और मजबूत होता है।" | Hindi (PM’s commentary) | Highlights the long-term societal benefits of cultural sensitivity: the strengthening of mutual understanding and brotherhood. |

---

## Multi-Lingual Reach and Accessibility
The communication was released by the Prime Minister’s Office in several languages to ensure broad regional accessibility across India. The availability of this message in the following languages underscores the commitment to the very diversity the message promotes:

*   Assamese
*   Bengali
*   Gujarati
*   Hindi
*   Malayalam
*   Manipuri
*   Marathi
*   Punjabi
*   Tamil
*   Telugu
*   Urdu

---

## Actionable Insights

### For Diplomatic and Social Relations
*   **Prioritize Cultural Competency:** To foster cooperation in any diverse setting, one must first invest in understanding the "Deshacharan" (local customs) and traditions of the respective groups.
*   **Trust-Building through Respect:** Trust is not an abstract concept but a result of demonstrated respect for the specific identities and cultures of others.
*   **Leadership Development:** Aspiring leaders should cultivate "Paravarajnah"—the wisdom to understand various perspectives and the humility to honor the diverse laws and traditions of the people they seek to lead.

### For Global Community Building
*   **Mutual Understanding as a Strategy:** To combat social fragmentation, organizations and individuals should focus on "mutual understanding" as a primary objective, using cultural education as a tool to build brotherhood.
*   **Universal Application:** The principles found in the Subhashitam are presented as timeless and universal, applicable to both local community interactions and global international relations.

mains_questions.question: The Prime Minister's emphasis on respecting diverse cultures, as highlighted by the Sanskrit Subhashitam, underscores its significance in contemporary society. Discuss how cultural diversity can be a source of strength for a nation and contribute to its soft power on the global stage.
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:**
The Prime Minister's sharing of a Sanskrit Subhashitam, emphasizing respect for diverse cultures, highlights a fundamental principle for societal harmony and international relations. This principle is crucial in understanding how cultural diversity can be both an internal strength and an external diplomatic asset.

**Cultural Diversity as a Source of National Strength:**
*   **National Integration and Unity:** Acknowledging and respecting varied cultural practices, languages, and traditions fosters a sense of belonging among diverse groups, strengthening national cohesion.
*   **Enrichment of Social Fabric:** Diversity brings a wealth of perspectives, arts, literature, cuisines, and knowledge systems, leading to a vibrant and dynamic society.
*   **Innovation and Creativity:** Different cultural viewpoints can spark new ideas, approaches, and solutions to challenges, driving progress in various fields.
*   **Tolerance and Mutual Understanding:** Exposure to diverse cultures within a nation promotes empathy, reduces prejudices, and builds a more inclusive society.

**Contribution to Soft Power on the Global Stage:**
*   **Enhanced Global Appeal and Influence:** A nation that celebrates its cultural diversity and respects others projects an image of openness and inclusivity, increasing its attractiveness and influence without coercion.
*   **Facilitating Diplomatic Relations:** Cultural exchange programs, festivals, and shared heritage create avenues for dialogue and cooperation, building stronger bilateral and multilateral ties.
*   **Attracting Tourism and Investment:** A rich and diverse cultural landscape draws tourists, fostering economic growth and promoting cross-cultural understanding.
*   **Projection of Values:** Promoting cultural respect globally aligns with universal values of peace, understanding, and human dignity, enhancing a nation's moral standing.
*   **Examples:** India's promotion of Yoga, Ayurveda, classical arts, and festivals globally exemplifies its soft power derived from cultural heritage.

**Conclusion:**
Respecting diverse cultures, as advocated by the Sanskrit Subhashitam, is not merely an ethical ideal but a strategic imperative. It fortifies a nation from within by fostering unity and enriches its global standing by enhancing its soft power, thereby contributing to a more harmonious and cooperative world order.

mains_questions.question: In an increasingly interconnected world, the principle of respecting diverse cultures is crucial for fostering global trust and cooperation. Analyze the ethical imperatives behind this principle and its implications for India's foreign policy.
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:**
The Prime Minister's message, rooted in a Sanskrit Subhashitam, underscores the profound importance of respecting diverse cultures. In a globalized era, this principle transcends mere courtesy, becoming a cornerstone for building trust, fostering cooperation, and shaping ethical foreign policy.

**Ethical Imperatives Behind Cultural Respect:**
*   **Universal Humanism:** Recognizing the inherent dignity and worth of every individual and community, irrespective of their cultural background. It promotes the idea of a shared humanity.
*   **Tolerance and Empathy:** Cultivating an understanding and acceptance of different worldviews, customs, and traditions, moving beyond ethnocentrism.
*   **Justice and Equity:** Ensuring that no culture is deemed superior or inferior, and advocating for the equal right of all cultures to exist, thrive, and contribute to the global tapestry.
*   **Peace and Harmony:** Cultural disrespect often fuels prejudice, discrimination, and conflict. Respect, conversely, lays the foundation for peaceful coexistence and conflict resolution.
*   **Preservation of Global Heritage:** Each culture represents a unique repository of human knowledge, creativity, and experience. Respect ensures their preservation for future generations.

**Implications for India's Foreign Policy:**
*   **"Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" (The World is One Family):** This ancient Indian philosophy, deeply embedded in its foreign policy, directly translates to respecting the diversity of nations and cultures as part of a larger global family.
*   **Multilateralism and Dialogue:** India actively participates in international forums, advocating for dialogue, mutual understanding, and consensus-building, which are predicated on cultural respect.
*   **Cultural Diplomacy and Soft Power:** India leverages its rich cultural heritage (e.g., Yoga, Ayurveda, classical arts, festivals) to build bridges, enhance its global image, and foster people-to-people connections.
*   **Non-Interference and Sovereignty:** Respect for diverse cultures extends to respecting the internal affairs and sovereign choices of other nations, avoiding imposition of one's own cultural norms.
*   **Addressing Global Challenges:** By fostering mutual understanding and trust through cultural respect, India can better collaborate with other nations on pressing global issues like climate change, terrorism, and sustainable development.
*   **Promoting Inclusivity:** India advocates for a more inclusive global order where diverse voices and perspectives are heard and valued, reflecting its own pluralistic society.

**Conclusion:**
The principle of respecting diverse cultures is not merely an ethical ideal but a pragmatic necessity for India's foreign policy. It underpins its vision for a peaceful, cooperative, and equitable world order, aligning its ancient wisdom with contemporary global challenges and opportunities.

title: Prime Minister attends the 50th Anniversary celebrations of Independence of Seychelles
content:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister attends the 50th Anniversary celebrations of Independence of Seychelles

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUN 2026 8:00AM by PIB Delhi

At the invitation of the President of Seychelles, H.E. Dr. Patrick Herminie, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today attended the 50th Anniversary celebrations of the Independence of Seychelles as the Guest of Honour. He is the first Indian Prime Minister to attend the Independence Day celebrations in Seychelles.

The Independence Day celebrations coincide with the marking of 50 years of the establishment of diplomatic ties between India and Seychelles. To commemorate these special occasions, contingents of Indian armed forces participated in the national parade held to mark the golden jubilee of the Independence of Seychelles. The Indian contingent comprised personnel from the Assam Rifles, the Indian Navy and an Indian Navy Marching Band, reflecting the longstanding defence partnership between the two countries. As part of the celebrations and in keeping with established tradition, Indian Naval Ships Tarkash and Ikshak docked at Port Victoria.

Prime Minister’s participation in the celebrations highlights the deep partnership and longstanding friendship between the two countries.

ai_content.summary:
# Briefing Document: Prime Minister’s Attendance at the 50th Anniversary of Seychelles Independence

## Executive Summary

On June 29, 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi attended the 50th Anniversary celebrations of the Independence of Seychelles as the Guest of Honour. This historic visit, conducted at the invitation of Seychelles President H.E. Dr. Patrick Herminie, marks the first time an Indian Prime Minister has attended the nation's Independence Day celebrations. The event serves as a dual milestone, celebrating both the golden jubilee of Seychelles' independence and the 50th anniversary of the establishment of formal diplomatic relations between India and Seychelles. The visit underscores a deepening strategic partnership, characterized by significant defense cooperation and a longstanding bilateral friendship.

---

## Detailed Analysis of Key Themes

### 1. Diplomatic and Historical Significance
The visit represents a pinnacle in the bilateral relationship between India and Seychelles. The year 2026 is of particular importance as it aligns two major milestones:
*   **The Golden Jubilee of Seychelles:** Celebrating 50 years of independence.
*   **Diplomatic Anniversary:** Celebrating 50 years of formal diplomatic ties between the two nations.

By serving as the Guest of Honour, the Prime Minister emphasizes India's role as a primary partner in the region and reaffirms the "deep partnership" that has evolved over the past five decades.

### 2. Strategic Defense Partnership
A central component of the celebrations was the visible demonstration of defense ties. The longstanding security relationship was highlighted through active participation in the national parade:
*   **Joint Participation:** Contingents from the Indian armed forces marched alongside local forces.
*   **Personnel Diversity:** The Indian contingent featured personnel from the **Assam Rifles**, the **Indian Navy**, and an **Indian Navy Marching Band**.
*   **Naval Presence:** In accordance with maritime tradition, two Indian Naval Ships—**INS Tarkash** and **INS Ikshak**—docked at Port Victoria for the occasion.

### 3. Regional Leadership and Presence
The Prime Minister’s status as the first Indian leader to attend this specific celebration highlights a proactive approach to Indian Ocean diplomacy. The presence of high-level representation and military assets (ships and marching contingents) projects India’s commitment to the security and sovereignty of Seychelles.

---

## Important Entities and Context

| Entity | Role/Significance |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Shri Narendra Modi** | Prime Minister of India; first Indian PM to attend Seychelles' Independence Day. |
| **H.E. Dr. Patrick Herminie** | President of Seychelles; extended the invitation to the Prime Minister. |
| **Assam Rifles & Indian Navy** | Military branches representing India in the Seychelles national parade. |
| **INS Tarkash & INS Ikshak** | Indian Naval Ships docked at Port Victoria to commemorate the golden jubilee. |
| **Port Victoria** | The site of the naval docking and a central location for the festivities. |

---

## Important Quotes and Context

> **"He is the first Indian Prime Minister to attend the Independence Day celebrations in Seychelles."**
*   **Context:** This statement highlights the unprecedented nature of the visit and the high priority placed on the India-Seychelles relationship by the current administration.

> **"The Independence Day celebrations coincide with the marking of 50 years of the establishment of diplomatic ties between India and Seychelles."**
*   **Context:** This underscores the historical synchronicity of the two nations' formal interactions, suggesting that India has been a partner since the very inception of Seychelles as a sovereign state.

> **"Prime Minister’s participation in the celebrations highlights the deep partnership and longstanding friendship between the two countries."**
*   **Context:** This serves as the core takeaway of the event, framing the military and diplomatic gestures as symbols of a broader, enduring alliance.

---

## Actionable Insights

*   **Strengthening Maritime Security:** The docking of INS Tarkash and INS Ikshak suggests continued opportunities for joint naval exercises and maritime domain awareness initiatives in the Indian Ocean.
*   **Leveraging Diplomatic Anniversaries:** The synchronization of the 50-year milestones provides a platform for both nations to launch new bilateral initiatives in trade, culture, and security.
*   **Defense Personnel Exchanges:** The inclusion of the Assam Rifles and the Navy Marching Band indicates a multifaceted defense relationship that extends beyond equipment sales to include ceremonial and personnel-based cooperation.
*   **High-Level Engagement:** The Prime Minister's presence as Guest of Honour sets a precedent for sustained high-level diplomatic engagement, which can be utilized to further strategic interests in the region.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of India-Seychelles relations in India's foreign policy, particularly in the context of its 'SAGAR' vision. Elaborate on the key areas of cooperation between the two countries.
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** Briefly introduce the historical and strategic ties between India and Seychelles, highlighting the recent 50th-anniversary celebrations of Seychelles' independence and diplomatic relations.

**Significance of India-Seychelles Relations:**
*   **Strategic Location:** Seychelles' crucial position in the Western Indian Ocean, vital for maritime security and trade routes.
*   **SAGAR Vision:** Alignment with India's 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) doctrine, emphasizing maritime cooperation, capacity building, and regional stability.
*   **Countering Piracy & Maritime Security:** Joint efforts to combat piracy, illegal fishing, and other maritime crimes.
*   **Geopolitical Balance:** India's presence helps maintain a balance of power in the Indian Ocean region.
*   **Diaspora:** Presence of a significant Indian diaspora fostering cultural and economic links.

**Key Areas of Cooperation:**
*   **Defence and Security:**
    *   Joint military exercises (e.g., LAMITIYE).
    *   Naval cooperation, port calls, hydrographic surveys.
    *   Capacity building and training for Seychelles' defence forces.
    *   Supply of defence equipment and patrol vessels.
*   **Economic Cooperation:**
    *   Trade and investment, particularly in tourism, infrastructure, and IT.
    *   Developmental assistance through Lines of Credit and grants.
*   **Developmental Partnership:**
    *   Infrastructure projects (e.g., housing, judicial buildings).
    *   Human resource development, scholarships, and training programs.
*   **People-to-People Ties:** Cultural exchanges, promotion of tourism.
*   **Multilateral Forums:** Cooperation in UN, Commonwealth, and other international bodies.

**Conclusion:** Reiterate that the robust India-Seychelles partnership is a cornerstone of India's Indian Ocean policy, contributing significantly to regional peace, security, and prosperity.

mains_questions.question: India's growing engagement with Indian Ocean Island States (IOIS) is crucial for its strategic interests. In this context, critically analyze the role of defence cooperation in strengthening India's ties with countries like Seychelles.
mains_questions.answer:
**Introduction:** Briefly state India's increasing focus on the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and the strategic importance of Indian Ocean Island States (IOIS) like Seychelles for India's maritime security and economic interests.

**Importance of IOIS for India's Strategic Interests:**
*   **Maritime Domain Awareness:** Enhancing surveillance and monitoring capabilities across the IOR.
*   **Chokepoint Security:** Safeguarding vital sea lanes of communication (SLOCs) and chokepoints.
*   **Countering Non-Traditional Threats:** Addressing piracy, terrorism, illegal fishing, and drug trafficking.
*   **SAGAR Vision:** Realizing the vision of a secure and prosperous Indian Ocean.
*   **Geopolitical Influence:** Counterbalancing the growing influence of other major powers in the region.

**Role of Defence Cooperation in Strengthening Ties:**
*   **Capacity Building:** Training, equipment supply, and infrastructure development for IOIS defence forces (e.g., coastal radar systems, patrol vessels).
*   **Joint Exercises:** Enhancing interoperability and mutual understanding through joint military and naval exercises.
*   **Maritime Security:** Collaborative efforts in surveillance, anti-piracy operations, and HADR (Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief).
*   **Information Sharing:** Exchange of intelligence and maritime domain information.
*   **Diplomatic Leverage:** Defence cooperation often serves as a strong pillar for broader diplomatic and economic engagement.
*   **Trust Building:** Fostering long-term trust and partnership through consistent support and engagement.

**Critical Analysis/Challenges:**
*   **Resource Constraints:** India's capacity to provide extensive defence assistance to all IOIS.
*   **Balancing Act:** Navigating the geopolitical complexities and interests of other global powers in the IOR.
*   **Sovereignty Concerns:** Ensuring that defence cooperation respects the sovereignty and strategic autonomy of IOIS.
*   **Sustainability:** Long-term maintenance and operationalization of supplied equipment and infrastructure.
*   **Comprehensive Approach:** Defence cooperation must be part of a broader engagement strategy encompassing economic, developmental, and cultural ties.

**Conclusion:** Conclude that defence cooperation is an indispensable tool for India to secure its strategic interests and foster robust partnerships with IOIS like Seychelles, contributing to a stable and secure Indian Ocean Region, provided it is pursued with a nuanced and comprehensive approach.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the constitutional provisions related to the oath or affirmation taken by Members of Parliament in India. What is the significance of this ceremony in upholding the democratic principles and the Constitution?
mains_questions.answer:
### Introduction
The oath-taking ceremony by Members of Parliament (MPs) is a fundamental ritual in India's parliamentary democracy, symbolizing their commitment to the nation and its foundational principles.

### Constitutional Provisions for Oath/Affirmation
1.  **Article 99:** Mandates that every member of either House of Parliament must, before taking their seat, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.
2.  **Third Schedule:** Prescribes the specific form of the oath/affirmation, which includes:
    *   Bearing true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established.
    *   Upholding the sovereignty and integrity of India.
    *   Faithfully discharging the duty upon which they are about to enter.
3.  **Administering Authority:** The oath is typically administered by the Presiding Officer of the respective House (Speaker for Lok Sabha, Chairman for Rajya Sabha) or a person appointed by them.
4.  **Consequence of Non-Compliance:** An MP cannot take their seat or participate in parliamentary proceedings until they have taken the oath. Failure to do so can lead to disqualification from sitting and voting.

### Significance of the Ceremony
1.  **Constitutional Allegiance:** It formally binds the MP to the Constitution, making it clear that their primary loyalty is to the supreme law of the land, not to any political party, ideology, or individual.
2.  **Upholding Sovereignty and Integrity:** The pledge to uphold India's sovereignty and integrity reinforces the MP's commitment to national unity and territorial inviolability.
3.  **Accountability and Duty:** It serves as a solemn reminder of the immense responsibility and duties that come with being a public representative, encouraging them to act in the best interests of the nation and its citizens.
4.  **Symbolic Importance:** The public nature of the ceremony underscores the transparency and democratic values of the parliamentary system, marking the formal entry of elected representatives into their legislative roles.
5.  **Ethical Foundation:** It lays down an ethical framework for parliamentary conduct, emphasizing integrity, impartiality, and dedication to public service.
6.  **Legal Prerequisite:** It is a mandatory legal requirement without which an individual cannot function as an MP, thus ensuring adherence to constitutional procedures.

### Conclusion
The oath or affirmation ceremony is more than a mere formality; it is a profound constitutional act that reinforces the democratic ethos, ensures allegiance to the Constitution, and sets the moral and legal compass for Members of Parliament in their legislative and representative capacities.

mains_questions.question: Examine the composition and powers of the Rajya Sabha, highlighting its role as a federal chamber in the Indian parliamentary system. How does it contribute to legislative scrutiny and representation of states?
mains_questions.answer:
### Introduction
The Rajya Sabha, or the Council of States, is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. It plays a crucial role in the country's bicameral legislature, primarily functioning as a representative body for the states and a house of legislative review.

### Composition of Rajya Sabha
1.  **Maximum Strength:** The Constitution limits the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha to 250 members.
2.  **Elected Members (238):** These members are representatives of the States and Union Territories. They are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and by an electoral college for Union Territories, through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
3.  **Nominated Members (12):** The President of India nominates 12 members who have special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service. This provision aims to bring expertise and diverse perspectives into parliamentary deliberations.
4.  **Permanent Body:** Unlike the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution. One-third of its members retire every two years, and elections are held to fill these vacancies.

### Powers of Rajya Sabha
1.  **Legislative Powers:** In most legislative matters, including ordinary bills and constitutional amendment bills, the Rajya Sabha enjoys co-equal powers with the Lok Sabha.
2.  **Financial Powers:** The Rajya Sabha has limited powers regarding Money Bills. A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and, once passed, is sent to the Rajya Sabha, which can only recommend amendments or delay it for a maximum of 14 days. The Lok Sabha is not bound by the Rajya Sabha's recommendations.
3.  **Executive Powers:** Members of the Rajya Sabha can ask questions to ministers, move resolutions, and participate in debates on government policies. However, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha.
4.  **Special Powers (Exclusive to Rajya Sabha):**
    *   **Article 249:** Empowers Parliament to make laws on a subject enumerated in the State List, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority declaring it necessary or expedient in the national interest.
    *   **Article 312:** Empowers Parliament to create new All India Services, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority declaring it necessary or expedient in the national interest.

### Role as a Federal Chamber and in Legislative Scrutiny
1.  **Representation of States:** As a 'Council of States,' the Rajya Sabha ensures that the interests and voices of individual states are represented at the national level, thereby upholding the federal structure of the Indian polity.
2.  **Check on Hasty Legislation:** It acts as a revising chamber, providing an opportunity for a second thought on legislation passed by the Lok Sabha. This prevents hasty or ill-considered legislation and allows for more thorough debate and scrutiny of bills.
3.  **Expertise and Deliberation:** The presence of nominated members, along with experienced politicians, enriches the quality of debates and brings diverse expertise to legislative processes.
4.  **Continuity in Legislation:** Being a permanent body, it ensures continuity in the legislative process, especially when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
5.  **Voice for Minorities and Regional Interests:** It provides a platform for smaller states and regional parties to articulate their concerns and influence national policy-making, which might otherwise be overshadowed in the Lok Sabha due to population-based representation.

### Conclusion
The Rajya Sabha is an indispensable component of India's parliamentary system. Its unique composition and special powers underscore its critical role in maintaining the federal balance, ensuring robust legislative scrutiny, and providing a platform for diverse representation, thereby strengthening democratic governance.
